# AGENTS.md

This repository holds `@local/dsh-software-factory`, a DSH (DeepSeek Harness)
Host plugin bundle: the `/factory` slash command, an 8-phase software-delivery
pipeline driven through DSH-native machinery, plus a Web-client right-sidebar
tab that observes pipeline progress.

## Layout

- `package.json` — bundle manifest (`dsh.bundle.patch`, `dsh.client` web section).
- `cordis.patch.yml` — the single Loader insert row (`id: software-factory`).
- `index.js` — Host half: Config schema (Standard Schema `~standard`), the
  `/factory` command, the `.factory.yml` project-override reader, and the
  `factory` session projection that derives progress from the session log.
- `client.js` — Web half (ModuleLoader factory): the right-sidebar "Factory"
  tab over the projection's wire view.
- `locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json` — Plugin Manager display metadata.
- `icon.svg` — card icon. `README.md` — full documentation, including the
  `.factory.yml` format.

## Conventions

- **Verification bar**: every change ends with `node --check` on each touched
  `.js` file plus a behavioral smoke run (see `.tmp` scratch in the settings
  repo); quote the real outputs in the report. Never claim success without
  same-turn on-disk evidence.
- **No agent git commits** in this repository. The user and the Lead review;
  they commit. Do not run `plugin_manager` here either: installation happens
  from the settings repo's session by the Lead/user.
- **Reinstall + restart**: after this package is (re)installed into a profile,
  the running Host keeps serving the old module generation until DSH restarts.
- **`.factory.yml`**: this repository may carry one (it does not today); the
  format is documented in README.md. It only affects `/factory` runs whose
  session workspace is this repository.
- **No machine-specific absolute paths** in any tracked file; resolve from
  environment or configuration.
- **Dependencies**: none at runtime. Host schemas are dependency-free
  facades over the protocols Cordis actually calls (`~standard.validate`,
  `schema.parse`); the client half imports React only through the browser
  module table and styles exclusively with `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens.

</system-reminder>

tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

<type>file</type>
<content>
1: /**
2:  * @local/dsh-software-factory — Host half.
3:  *
4:  * Registers the `/factory <request>` human command. The command steers one
5:  * model-visible user message into the receiving agent (the same mechanism
6:  * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode` uses for `/plan [message]`): a structured
7:  * pipeline prompt for the 8 delivery phases below, followed by the user's
8:  * request. The agent then executes the pipeline with DSH-native machinery —
9:  * todo/plan facilities, file tools, optional subagent delegation, the shell
10:  * tool, and background jobs — while narrating one compact status line per
11:  * phase transition.
12:  *
13:  * Progress observability: the `factory` session projection folds the
14:  * session log's `assistant/message` events, matching ONLY lines that start
15:  * with the plugin's own narration contract (`[factory] phase <n>/8 <key>:
16:  * <status>`), and publishes a wire view per session. The Web client half
17:  * (client.js, right-sidebar tab) reads it through the shipped session
18:  * binding (`sessions.binding(id).session.projections.faceOf('factory')`) —
19:  * the same host→client shape the shipped plan-mode and goal plugins use.
20:  * The projection is registered through the optional `sessionProjections`
21:  * service, so profiles without it keep the command fully functional.
22:  *
23:  * The plugin itself owns no pipeline state: the steered message, the agent's
24:  * tool calls, their results, and the derived projection all reconstruct
25:  * from the session log, so fork/resume/replay reproduce the run. This keeps
26:  * the "session log is the only source of truth" practice of the Harness.
27:  *
28:  * Per-project overrides: when `/factory` runs, the plugin reads
29:  * `.factory.yml` from the session workspace root — resolved exactly the way
30:  * the shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions` resolves instruction
31:  * files: `agent.session.header.cwd ?? process.cwd()` for the root, then the
32:  * optional `fs` service (`ctx.get('fs')`: `resolve(path, { cwd, signal })` →
33:  * `stat(target, signal)` → `readText(target, signal)`) with a `node:fs`
34:  * fallback when the service is absent. The file may override the six phase
35:  * toggles and append per-phase prompt text (see `parseFactoryYml`); the
36:  * plugin row Config stays the global default layer and keeps command lists
37:  * and the deploy gate to itself. A missing file changes nothing; an invalid
38:  * file fails loudly with the file named.
39:  *
40:  * Contracts coded against (verified by inspection of the installed Harness):
41:  * - `ctx.commands.register({ name, description, input: { hint, attachments },
42:  *    recordInput, handler })` from the `commands` service
43:  *    (@deepseek-ai/dsh-commands). The handler receives
44:  *    `{ agent, rawInput, attachments, signal }` and its return value is
45:  *    awaited (`await withAbort(Promise.resolve(output), signal)`); it returns
46:  *    `{ kind: 'success', text? }` or `{ kind: 'error', text }`.
47:  * - `agent.steer(userMessage)` (dsh-agent-loop ReactLoopAgent) inserts the
48:  *    message for the next step AND wakes the driver; the message shape is
49:  *    `{ role: 'user', content: ContentBlock[], source: { kind: 'user' },
50:  *    id }` as produced by dsh-llm's `createUserMessage` (the id brand is a
51:  *    compile-time no-op, so a locally built frozen object is identical).
52:  * - `ctx.inject(['commands'], callback)` (cordis Context.inject) starts a
53:  *    child plugin only while the optional `commands` service exists and
54:  *    returns its fiber, whose `dispose()` is this plugin's cleanup. The
55:  *    `fs` service is looked up dynamically with `ctx.get('fs')` (the
56:  *    dsh-agent-instructions pattern): it is the preferred read path, and the
57:  *    node:fs fallback keeps the command working when it is absent.
58:  * - `export const Config` is consumed through the Standard Schema
59:  *    `~standard.validate` protocol (cordis `resolveConfig`), so the schema
60:  *    below is a dependency-free implementation of that contract.
61:  */
62: import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
63: import { readFile as nodeReadFile, stat as nodeStat } from 'node:fs/promises';
64: import { join } from 'node:path';
65: 
66: /**
67:  * The fixed pipeline identity: eight phases, in order. `key` is the slug used
68:  * in status lines; `toggle` names the Config boolean that enables the phase
69:  * (phase 1 capture is the request itself and is always enabled; phase 6
70:  * deploy is additionally gated on a configured deploy command).
71:  */
72: const PHASES = [
73:   { key: 'capture', name: 'Capture the request', toggle: null },
74:   { key: 'plan', name: 'Plan the tasks', toggle: 'plan' },
75:   { key: 'implement', name: 'Implement the tasks', toggle: 'implement' },
76:   { key: 'guardrails', name: 'Run guardrails', toggle: 'guardrails' },
77:   { key: 'test', name: 'Test the implementation', toggle: 'test' },
78:   { key: 'deploy', name: 'Deploy to test environment', toggle: 'deploy' },
79:   { key: 'regression', name: 'Run regression tests', toggle: 'regression' },
80:   { key: 'evaluate', name: 'Evaluate and report', toggle: 'evaluate' },
81: ];
82: 
83: const TOP_LEVEL_KEYS = new Set([
84:   'plan',
85:   'implement',
86:   'guardrails',
87:   'test',
88:   'deploy',
89:   'regression',
90:   'evaluate',
91:   'guardrailCommand',
92:   'testCommand',
93:   'regressionCommand',
94:   'subagentImplementation',
95: ]);
96: 
97: /** The per-project file this plugin reads from the session workspace root. */
98: const PROJECT_FILE_NAME = '.factory.yml';
99: 
100: /** Phase toggles a `.factory.yml` may override (deploy stays plugin-Config-only). */
101: const PROJECT_TOGGLE_KEYS = new Set([
102:   'plan',
103:   'implement',
104:   'guardrails',
105:   'test',
106:   'regression',
107:   'evaluate',
108: ]);
109: 
110: /** Phases a `.factory.yml` `phasePrompts` entry may target (deploy prompts DO apply). */
111: const PROJECT_PROMPT_KEYS = new Set([
112:   'plan',
113:   'implement',
114:   'guardrails',
115:   'test',
116:   'deploy',
117:   'regression',
118:   'evaluate',
119: ]);
120: 
121: /** Top-level keys allowed in a `.factory.yml`. */
122: const PROJECT_TOP_KEYS = new Set(['phases', 'phasePrompts']);
123: 
124: /** Upper bound for `.factory.yml` size — it becomes part of the steered prompt. */
125: const PROJECT_FILE_MAX_CHARS = 65536;
126: 
127: /**
128:  * The session-projection key whose wire view the Web client's right-sidebar
129:  * tab reads (`sessions.binding(id).session.projections.faceOf('factory')`).
130:  */
131: const FACTORY_PROJECTION_KEY = 'factory';
132: 
133: /**
134:  * The narration contract this plugin's prompt imposes on the agent. Only
135:  * lines matching this pattern at line start fold projection state, so
136:  * unrelated text (including tool output echoing the prompt) can never be
137:  * misparsed as progress.
138:  */
139: const STATUS_LINE_PATTERN = /^\[factory\] phase ([1-8])\/8 ([a-z]+): (.*)$/;
140: 
141: /** Phase statuses the projection tracks. */
142: const PHASE_STATUSES = new Set(['pending', 'active', 'done', 'skipped', 'failed']);
143: 
144: /**
145:  * Build the initial projection state: eight pending phases, no run.
146:  * @returns {{running: boolean, phases: {n: number, key: string,
147:  *   status: string, text: string | null}[], lastLine: string | null}}
148:  */
149: function emptyProjectionState() {
150:   return {
151:     running: false,
152:     phases: PHASES.map((phase, index) => ({
153:       n: index + 1,
154:       key: phase.key,
155:       status: 'pending',
156:       text: null,
157:     })),
158:     lastLine: null,
159:   };
160: }
161: 
162: /**
163:  * Fold one narration line into a fresh state (or the same reference when
164:  * nothing changes). Deterministic and clock-free: replay-safe.
165:  * @param {ReturnType<emptyProjectionState>} state current state.
166:  * @param {number} n phase number from the line (1-8).
167:  * @param {string} key phase key from the line.
168:  * @param {string} text status text after the colon.
169:  * @param {string} rawLine the full verbatim line.
170:  * @returns {ReturnType<emptyProjectionState>} next state.
171:  */
172: function foldStatusLine(state, n, key, text, rawLine) {
173:   if (PHASES[n - 1].key !== key) return state;
174:   let phases = state.phases.map((phase) => ({ ...phase }));
175:   // A phase-1 line after a finished run starts a fresh run.
176:   if (n === 1 && !state.running && phases[0].status !== 'pending') {
177:     phases = emptyProjectionState().phases;
178:   }
179:   // Progression: entering phase n closes every earlier open phase as done.
180:   for (let i = 0; i < n - 1; i += 1) {
181:     if (phases[i].status === 'active' || phases[i].status === 'pending') {
182:       phases[i] = { ...phases[i], status: 'done' };
183:     }
184:   }
185:   const lower = text.toLowerCase();
186:   const status = lower.includes('skip')
187:     ? 'skipped'
188:     : (lower.includes('fail') || lower.includes('error') || lower.includes('blocked'))
189:       ? 'failed'
190:       : n === PHASES.length ? 'done' : 'active';
191:   phases[n - 1] = { ...phases[n - 1], status, text };
192:   const final = phases[PHASES.length - 1].status;
193:   return {
194:     running: final !== 'done' && final !== 'failed' && final !== 'skipped',
195:     phases,
196:     lastLine: rawLine,
197:   };
198: }
199: 
200: /** Assert-and-return the projection state shape (a `.parse` facade body). */
201: function validateProjectionState(input) {
202:   if (typeof input !== 'object' || input === null || Array.isArray(input)) {
203:     throw new Error('factory projection state must be an object');
204:   }
205:   if (typeof input.running !== 'boolean') throw new Error('factory projection state "running" must be a boolean');
206:   if (!Array.isArray(input.phases) || input.phases.length !== PHASES.length) {
207:     throw new Error(`factory projection state "phases" must be an array of ${PHASES.length} entries`);
208:   }
209:   input.phases.forEach((phase, index) => {
210:     if (typeof phase !== 'object' || phase === null) throw new Error(`factory projection phase ${index + 1} must be an object`);
211:     if (phase.n !== index + 1 || phase.key !== PHASES[index].key) {
212:       throw new Error(`factory projection phase ${index + 1} identity mismatch`);
213:     }
214:     if (!PHASE_STATUSES.has(phase.status)) throw new Error(`factory projection phase ${index + 1} has unknown status "${String(phase.status)}"`);
215:     if (phase.text !== null && typeof phase.text !== 'string') throw new Error(`factory projection phase ${index + 1} text must be a string or null`);
216:   });
217:   if (input.lastLine !== null && typeof input.lastLine !== 'string') {
218:     throw new Error('factory projection state "lastLine" must be a string or null');
219:   }
220:   return input;
221: }
222: 
223: /**
224:  * The factory progress projection. The session-projection registry only
225:  * calls `schema.parse(...)` on state and wire values, so the schemas below
226:  * are dependency-free `{ parse }` facades (the same trick as `Config`'s
227:  * `~standard`, one protocol level up). The wire view reaches the Web client
228:  * through the shipped session binding (`projections.faceOf('factory')`) —
229:  * the exact host→client shape plan-mode and goal use.
230:  */
231: const factoryProjectionDefinition = {
232:   key: FACTORY_PROJECTION_KEY,
233:   stateVersion: 1,
234:   stateSchema: { parse: validateProjectionState },
235:   init: () => emptyProjectionState(),
236:   apply: (state, event) => {
237:     if (event.type !== 'assistant/message') return state;
238:     const content = event.data?.message?.content;
239:     if (!Array.isArray(content)) return state;
240:     const text = content
241:       .filter((block) => block?.type === 'text' && typeof block.text === 'string')
242:       .map((block) => block.text)
243:       .join('\n');
244:     let next = state;
245:     for (const line of text.split('\n')) {
246:       const trimmed = line.trim();
247:       if (trimmed === '') continue;
248:       const match = STATUS_LINE_PATTERN.exec(trimmed);
249:       if (!match) continue;
250:       next = foldStatusLine(next, Number(match[1]), match[2], match[3], trimmed);
251:     }
252:     return next;
253:   },
254:   wire: {
255:     viewSchema: { parse: validateProjectionState },
256:     view: (state) => ({
257:       running: state.running,
258:       phases: state.phases.map((phase) => ({ ...phase })),
259:       lastLine: state.lastLine,
260:     }),
261:   },
262: };
263: 
264: /**
265:  * Recursively freeze plain data (arrays/objects) in place, mirroring the
266:  * immutable-message invariant of dsh-llm's message constructors.
267:  * @param {unknown} value
268:  * @returns {unknown} the same reference, frozen.
269:  */
270: function deepFreeze(value) {
271:   if (value !== null && (typeof value === 'object' || Array.isArray(value))) {
272:     for (const child of Object.values(value)) deepFreeze(child);
273:     Object.freeze(value);
274:   }
275:   return value;
276: }
277: 
278: /**
279:  * Read a boolean option.
280:  * @param {Record<string, unknown>} raw owner object of the field.
281:  * @param {string} name field name for diagnostics.
282:  * @param {boolean} fallback value used when the field is absent.
283:  * @returns {boolean}
284:  */
285: function readBoolean(raw, name, fallback) {
286:   const value = raw[name] === undefined ? fallback : raw[name];
287:   if (typeof value !== 'boolean') {
288:     throw new TypeError(`software-factory config "${name}" must be a boolean`);
289:   }
290:   return value;
291: }
292: 
293: /**
294:  * Read a command option: one non-empty string or an array of them,
295:  * normalized to a frozen array of strings.
296:  * @param {Record<string, unknown>} raw owner object of the field.
297:  * @param {string} name field name for diagnostics.
298:  * @param {readonly string[]} fallback value used when the field is absent.
299:  * @returns {readonly string[]}
300:  */
301: function readCommands(raw, name, fallback) {
302:   const value = raw[name] === undefined ? fallback : raw[name];
303:   const list = typeof value === 'string' ? [value] : value;
304:   if (
305:     !Array.isArray(list)
306:     || list.some((entry) => typeof entry !== 'string' || entry.trim() === '')
307:   ) {
308:     throw new TypeError(
309:       `software-factory config "${name}" must be a non-empty command string or an array of non-empty command strings`,
310:     );
311:   }
312:   return Object.freeze([...list]);
313: }

315: /**
316:  * Validate and normalize the plugin config. Unknown keys fail at activation
317:  * (the plan-mode `resolveConfig` pattern) so typos never silently disable a
318:  * phase.
319:  *
320:  * @param {unknown} input raw row config; `{}`/`undefined` selects defaults.
321:  * @returns {Readonly<{plan: boolean, implement: boolean, guardrails: boolean,
322:  *   test: boolean, regression: boolean, evaluate: boolean,
323:  *   subagentImplementation: boolean, deploy: {enabled: boolean, command: readonly string[]},
324:  *   guardrailCommand: readonly string[], testCommand: readonly string[],
325:  *   regressionCommand: readonly string[]}>}
326:  */
327: function resolveConfig(input) {
328:   const raw = input === undefined || input === null ? {} : input;
329:   if (typeof raw !== 'object' || Array.isArray(raw)) {
330:     throw new TypeError('software-factory config must be an object');
331:   }
332:   const unknown = Object.keys(raw).filter((key) => !TOP_LEVEL_KEYS.has(key));
333:   if (unknown.length > 0) {
334:     throw new Error(
335:       `software-factory config has unknown key(s) ${unknown.join(', ')} — allowed keys: ${[...TOP_LEVEL_KEYS].join(', ')}`,
336:     );
337:   }
338:   const deployRaw = raw.deploy === undefined ? {} : raw.deploy;
339:   if (typeof deployRaw !== 'object' || deployRaw === null || Array.isArray(deployRaw)) {
340:     throw new TypeError('software-factory config "deploy" must be an object');
341:   }
342:   const deployUnknown = Object.keys(deployRaw).filter((key) => key !== 'enabled' && key !== 'command');
343:   if (deployUnknown.length > 0) {
344:     throw new TypeError('software-factory config "deploy" allows only "enabled" and "command"');
345:   }
346:   return Object.freeze({
347:     plan: readBoolean(raw, 'plan', true),
348:     implement: readBoolean(raw, 'implement', true),
349:     guardrails: readBoolean(raw, 'guardrails', true),
350:     test: readBoolean(raw, 'test', true),
351:     regression: readBoolean(raw, 'regression', true),
352:     evaluate: readBoolean(raw, 'evaluate', true),
353:     subagentImplementation: readBoolean(raw, 'subagentImplementation', true),
354:     deploy: Object.freeze({
355:       enabled: readBoolean(deployRaw, 'enabled', false),
356:       command: readCommands(deployRaw, 'command', []),
357:     }),
358:     guardrailCommand: readCommands(raw, 'guardrailCommand', []),
359:     testCommand: readCommands(raw, 'testCommand', []),
360:     regressionCommand: readCommands(raw, 'regressionCommand', []),
361:   });
362: }

364: /**
365:  * The plugin's Config schema, implementing the Standard Schema `~standard`
366:  * protocol that cordis `resolveConfig` calls (`Config['~standard'].validate`).
367:  * Dependency-free on purpose: a local bundle must not need zod or Schemastery
368:  * installed beside it. The Settings/Config-inspect surfaces that project
369:  * known schema vendors will not render a form for this schema; the row config
370:  * in `cordis.patch.yml` remains the declarative way to configure the plugin.
371:  */
372: export const Config = {
373:   '~standard': {
374:     version: 1,
375:     vendor: '@local/dsh-software-factory',
376:     validate(raw) {
377:       try {
378:         return { value: resolveConfig(raw) };
379:       } catch (error) {
380:         return {
381:           issues: [
382:             {
383:               message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
384:             },
385:           ],
386:         };
387:       }
388:     },
389:   },
390: };

392: /**
393:  * Render a numbered command list for the prompt.
394:  * @param {readonly string[]} commands
395:  * @returns {string} markdown lines, empty when nothing is configured.
396:  */
397: function renderCommandList(commands) {
398:   if (commands.length === 0) return '';
399:   return commands.map((command, index) => `${index + 1}. \`${command}\``).join('\n');
400: }

402: /**
403:  * Whether the deploy phase may run: it must be enabled AND name a command.
404:  * Deploying is the one phase that is off until explicitly configured.
405:  */
406: function deployActive(resolved) {
407:   return resolved.deploy.enabled && resolved.deploy.command.length > 0;
408: }

410: /**
411:  * Parse the `.factory.yml` subset. Dependency-free on purpose; the supported
412:  * grammar (documented in README) is exactly:
413:  *
414:  * - optional blank lines and `#` comments anywhere;
415:  * - two top-level mapping headers `phases:` and `phasePrompts:` (each at
416:  *   most once, nothing after the colon);
417:  * - nested entries at one consistent indentation (spaces only — tabs are an
418:  *   error), `key: value` on a single line;
419:  * - `phases.<key>`: `plan|implement|guardrails|test|regression|evaluate` =
420:  *   `true` or `false` (exactly; `yes`/`True` are errors);
421:  * - `phasePrompts.<key>`: `plan|implement|guardrails|test|deploy|
422:  *   regression|evaluate` = a string — plain scalar (trailing ` # comment`
423:  *   stripped), single-quoted (only `''` escape), double-quoted (only `\"`,
424:  *   `\\`, `\n`, `\t` escapes), or a block scalar `|` / `|-` (literal) or
425:  *   `>` / `>-` (folded: paragraph lines joined with one space, blank lines
426:  *   collapse to one paragraph break, deeper-indented lines stay verbatim);
427:  *   `|`/`>` keep one trailing newline, `|-`/`>-` strip it;
428:  * - nothing else: no lists, anchors, tags, multi-document input, multi-line
429:  *   plain scalars, or deeper nesting.
430:  *
431:  * Every violation throws an Error naming the file and line.
432:  *
433:  * @param {string} text raw file content (UTF-8; BOM and CRLF tolerated).
434:  * @param {{displayName?: string}} options error-naming options.
435:  * @returns {Readonly<{phases: Readonly<Record<string, boolean>>,
436:  *   phasePrompts: Readonly<Record<string, string>>}>}
437:  */
438: export function parseFactoryYml(text, options = {}) {
439:   const displayName = options.displayName ?? PROJECT_FILE_NAME;
440:   const fail = (lineNumber, detail) => new Error(`${displayName} line ${lineNumber}: ${detail}`);
441:   const source = text.charCodeAt(0) === 0xfeff ? text.slice(1) : text;
442:   const lines = source.split(/\r\n|\n|\r/);
443:   const phases = {};
444:   const phasePrompts = {};
445:   const seenTop = new Set();
446:   let topKey = null;
447:   let childIndent = -1;
448: 
449:   /** Split a line into its space indentation and content; tabs are an error. */
450:   const splitIndent = (raw, lineNumber) => {
451:     const match = /^([ \t]*)(.*)$/.exec(raw);
452:     if (match[1].includes('\t')) {
453:       throw fail(lineNumber, 'tabs are not allowed in indentation; use spaces');
454:     }
455:     return { indent: match[1].length, content: match[2] };
456:   };
457: 
458:   /** Strip a trailing comment (` # …`) from an unquoted scalar. */
459:   const stripComment = (scalar) => {
460:     for (let i = 0; i < scalar.length; i += 1) {
461:       if (scalar[i] !== '#') continue;
462:       if (i === 0 || scalar[i - 1] === ' ' || scalar[i - 1] === '\t') return scalar.slice(0, i);
463:     }
464:     return scalar;
465:   };
466: 
467:   /** Parse a single-line quoted string value. */
468:   const parseQuoted = (rest, lineNumber, childKey) => {
469:     if (rest.startsWith("'")) {
470:       const match = /^'((?:[^']|'')*)'(.*)$/.exec(rest);
471:       if (!match) throw fail(lineNumber, `"${childKey}" has an unterminated single-quoted value`);
472:       if (match[2].trim() !== '') {
473:         throw fail(lineNumber, `"${childKey}" has unexpected content after the closing quote`);
474:       }
475:       return match[1].replace(/''/g, "'");
476:     }
477:     const match = /^"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"(.*)$/.exec(rest);
478:     if (!match) throw fail(lineNumber, `"${childKey}" has an unterminated double-quoted value`);
479:     if (match[2].trim() !== '') {
480:       throw fail(lineNumber, `"${childKey}" has unexpected content after the closing quote`);
481:     }
482:     return match[1].replace(/\\(.)/g, (whole, escaped) => {
483:       switch (escaped) {
484:         case '"': return '"';
485:         case '\\': return '\\';
486:         case 'n': return '\n';
487:         case 't': return '\t';
488:         default:
489:           throw fail(lineNumber, `"${childKey}" uses unsupported escape "\\${escaped}" (supported: \\" \\\\ \\n \\t)`);
490:       }
491:     });
492:   };
493: 
494:   /** Collect and render a `|`/`|-`/`>`/`>-` block scalar starting after `index`. */
495:   const parseBlockScalar = (indicator, lines, index, nestedIndent, headerLineNumber) => {
496:     const collected = [];
497:     let contentIndent = -1;
498:     let i = index + 1;
499:     while (i < lines.length) {
500:       const raw = lines[i];
501:       if (raw.trim() === '') {
502:         collected.push('');
503:         i += 1;
504:         continue;
505:       }
506:       const { indent, content } = splitIndent(raw, i + 1);
507:       if (indent <= nestedIndent) break;
508:       if (contentIndent === -1) contentIndent = indent;
509:       if (indent < contentIndent) {
510:         throw fail(i + 1, `inconsistent block-scalar indentation (expected ${contentIndent} spaces)`);
511:       }
512:       collected.push(`${' '.repeat(indent - contentIndent)}${content}`);
513:       i += 1;
514:     }
515:     while (collected.length > 0 && collected[collected.length - 1] === '') collected.pop();
516:     if (collected.length === 0) {
517:       throw fail(headerLineNumber, `block scalar "${indicator}" has no content`);
518:     }
519:     let value;
520:     if (indicator === '|' || indicator === '|-') {
521:       value = collected.join('\n');
522:       if (indicator === '|') value += '\n';
523:     } else {
524:       const out = [];
525:       let paragraph = [];
526:       const flush = () => {
527:         if (paragraph.length > 0) {
528:           out.push(paragraph.join(' '));
529:           paragraph = [];
530:         }
531:       };
532:       for (const line of collected) {
533:         if (line === '') {
534:           flush();
535:           continue;
536:         }
537:         if (line.startsWith(' ')) {
538:           flush();
539:           out.push(line);
540:           continue;
541:         }
542:         paragraph.push(line);
543:       }
544:       flush();
545:       value = out.join('\n');
546:       if (indicator === '>') value += '\n';
547:     }
548:     return { value, nextIndex: i };
549:   };
550: 
551:   /** Parse one `key: rest` child entry at `index`; returns value + next index. */
552:   const parseChildValue = (currentTop, childKey, rest, index, nestedIndent) => {
553:     const lineNumber = index + 1;
554:     const indicator = stripComment(rest).trim();
555:     if (indicator === '|' || indicator === '|-' || indicator === '>' || indicator === '>-') {
556:       return parseBlockScalar(indicator, lines, index, nestedIndent, lineNumber);
557:     }
558:     const trimmed = rest.trim();
559:     if (currentTop === 'phases') {
560:       const boolText = stripComment(trimmed).trim();
561:       if (boolText !== 'true' && boolText !== 'false') {
562:         throw fail(lineNumber, `phases.${childKey} must be true or false (got "${boolText}")`);
563:       }
564:       return { value: boolText === 'true', nextIndex: index + 1 };
565:     }
566:     if (trimmed === '') throw fail(lineNumber, `"${childKey}" is missing a value`);
567:     if (trimmed.startsWith("'") || trimmed.startsWith('"')) {
568:       return { value: parseQuoted(trimmed, lineNumber, childKey), nextIndex: index + 1 };
569:     }
570:     const plain = stripComment(trimmed).trim();
571:     if (plain === '') throw fail(lineNumber, `"${childKey}" is missing a value`);
572:     return { value: plain, nextIndex: index + 1 };
573:   };
574: 
575:   let i = 0;
576:   while (i < lines.length) {
577:     const raw = lines[i];
578:     const trimmedRaw = raw.trim();
579:     if (trimmedRaw === '' || trimmedRaw.startsWith('#')) {
580:       i += 1;
581:       continue;
582:     }
583:     const { indent, content } = splitIndent(raw, i + 1);
584:     if (indent === 0) {
585:       topKey = null;
586:       childIndent = -1;
587:       const entry = /^([^\s:]+):\s*(.*)$/.exec(content);
588:       if (!entry) throw fail(i + 1, `expected a "key:" line, got "${content}"`);
589:       const [, key, rest] = entry;
590:       if (!PROJECT_TOP_KEYS.has(key)) {
591:         throw fail(i + 1, `unknown top-level key "${key}" — allowed keys: ${[...PROJECT_TOP_KEYS].join(', ')}`);
592:       }
593:       if (seenTop.has(key)) throw fail(i + 1, `duplicate top-level key "${key}"`);
594:       if (stripComment(rest).trim() !== '') {
595:         throw fail(i + 1, `"${key}:" must be a mapping header with nothing after the colon`);
596:       }
597:       seenTop.add(key);
598:       topKey = key;
599:       i += 1;
600:       continue;
601:     }
602:     if (topKey === null) throw fail(i + 1, 'unexpected indentation (no open mapping)');
603:     if (childIndent === -1) childIndent = indent;
604:     if (indent !== childIndent) {
605:       throw fail(i + 1, `inconsistent indentation: expected ${childIndent} space(s), found ${indent}`);
606:     }
607:     const entry = /^([^\s:]+):\s*(.*)$/.exec(content);
608:     if (!entry) throw fail(i + 1, `expected "key: value", got "${content}"`);
609:     const [, childKey, rest] = entry;
610:     const allowed = topKey === 'phases' ? PROJECT_TOGGLE_KEYS : PROJECT_PROMPT_KEYS;
611:     if (!allowed.has(childKey)) {
612:       throw fail(i + 1, `unknown key "${childKey}" under "${topKey}" — allowed keys: ${[...allowed].join(', ')}`);
613:     }
614:     const parsed = parseChildValue(topKey, childKey, rest, i, childIndent);
615:     if (topKey === 'phases') phases[childKey] = parsed.value;
616:     else phasePrompts[childKey] = parsed.value;
617:     i = parsed.nextIndex;
618:   }
619:   return Object.freeze({
620:     phases: Object.freeze({ ...phases }),
621:     phasePrompts: Object.freeze({ ...phasePrompts }),
622:   });
623: }

625: /**
626:  * Read `.factory.yml` from the session workspace root. Returns empty
627:  * overrides when the file is absent; throws a named-file Error when it is
628:  * too large or invalid.
629:  *
630:  * The root and read path follow the shipped dsh-agent-instructions pattern:
631:  * `agent.session.header.cwd ?? process.cwd()`, the `fs` service when
632:  * present (`resolve` → `stat` → `readText`, abort-aware), `node:fs`
633:  * otherwise.
634:  *
635:  * @param {import('@deepseek-ai/cordis').Context} ctx plugin context.
636:  * @param {{session?: {header?: {cwd?: string}}}} agent the receiving agent.
637:  * @param {AbortSignal | undefined} signal command abort signal.
638:  * @returns {Promise<Readonly<{phases: Record<string, boolean>,
639:  *   phasePrompts: Record<string, string>}>>}
640:  */
641: async function loadProjectOverrides(ctx, agent, signal) {
642:   const cwd = agent?.session?.header?.cwd ?? process.cwd();
643:   const displayName = `${PROJECT_FILE_NAME} (workspace root ${cwd})`;
644:   const empty = Object.freeze({ phases: Object.freeze({}), phasePrompts: Object.freeze({}) });
645:   const fileSystem = typeof ctx?.get === 'function' ? ctx.get('fs') : undefined;
646:   let text;
647:   if (fileSystem !== undefined) {
648:     const target = await fileSystem.resolve(PROJECT_FILE_NAME, {
649:       cwd,
650:       ...(signal === undefined ? {} : { signal }),
651:     });
652:     signal?.throwIfAborted();
653:     const info = await fileSystem.stat(target, signal);
654:     signal?.throwIfAborted();
655:     if (info === undefined || info.type !== 'file') return empty;
656:     text = await fileSystem.readText(target, signal);
657:   } else {
658:     const path = join(cwd, PROJECT_FILE_NAME);
659:     try {
660:       const info = await nodeStat(path, signal === undefined ? undefined : { signal });
661:       if (!info.isFile()) return empty;
662:     } catch (error) {
663:       if (error && typeof error === 'object' && (error.code === 'ENOENT' || error.code === 'ENOTDIR')) return empty;
664:       throw error;
665:     }
666:     text = await nodeReadFile(path, { encoding: 'utf8', ...(signal === undefined ? {} : { signal }) });
667:   }
668:   signal?.throwIfAborted();
669:   if (text.length > PROJECT_FILE_MAX_CHARS) {
670:     throw new Error(`${displayName}: file is too large (${text.length} chars; max ${PROJECT_FILE_MAX_CHARS})`);
671:   }
672:   return parseFactoryYml(text, { displayName });
673: }

675: /**
676:  * Merge plugin row Config (defaults) with `.factory.yml` (project overrides):
677:  * file phase toggles win, command lists and the deploy gate stay
678:  * plugin-Config-only, file phasePrompts attach verbatim.
679:  *
680:  * @param {ReturnType<resolveConfig>} resolved plugin row config.
681:  * @param {{phases?: Record<string, boolean>, phasePrompts?: Record<string, string>}} project
682:  *   parsed `.factory.yml` (or empty).
683:  * @returns {Readonly<ReturnType<resolveConfig> & {phasePrompts: Readonly<Record<string, string>>}>}
684:  */
685: export function applyProjectOverrides(resolved, project) {
686:   const phases = project?.phases ?? {};
687:   const phasePrompts = project?.phasePrompts ?? {};
688:   return Object.freeze({
689:     ...resolved,
690:     plan: phases.plan ?? resolved.plan,
691:     implement: phases.implement ?? resolved.implement,
692:     guardrails: phases.guardrails ?? resolved.guardrails,
693:     test: phases.test ?? resolved.test,
694:     regression: phases.regression ?? resolved.regression,
695:     evaluate: phases.evaluate ?? resolved.evaluate,
696:     phasePrompts: Object.freeze({ ...phasePrompts }),
697:   });
698: }

700: /**
701:  * Build the full pipeline prompt steered into the agent.
702:  * @param {ReturnType<typeof applyProjectOverrides>} resolved effective config
703:  *   (plugin row Config merged with `.factory.yml` overrides + phasePrompts).
704:  * @param {string} request the user's raw request text (already trimmed).
705:  * @returns {string} markdown prompt.
706:  */
707: function buildPipelinePrompt(resolved, request) {
708:   const lines = [];
709:   lines.push('# Software factory — 8-phase delivery pipeline');
710:   lines.push('');
711:   lines.push(
712:     'You are running the software-factory pipeline. Work through the eight phases below strictly in order, for the user request stated at the end of this message. The pipeline is executed with DSH-native machinery only — the session\'s real tools and logs are the record of the run.',
713:   );
714:   lines.push('');
715:   lines.push('Ground rules:');
716:   lines.push('');
717:   lines.push(
718:     '- Emit one compact status line when you ENTER each phase (with your intent) and one when you LEAVE it (with the outcome), in exactly this form: `[factory] phase <n>/8 <key>: <short status>` — for example `[factory] phase 3/8 implement: 3 tasks done`.',
719:   );
720:   lines.push(
721:     '- Never skip an enabled phase. If a phase fails, fix and retry within that phase; if it truly cannot pass, stop and report the failure honestly instead of moving on silently.',
722:   );
723:   lines.push(
724:     '- A disabled phase is still announced: `[factory] phase <n>/8 <key>: skipped (disabled by configuration)`.',
725:   );
726:   lines.push(
727:     '- Report command results honestly: a non-zero exit code is a failure, whatever the output looks like. Quote exit codes.',
728:   );
729:   lines.push(
730:     '- Do not restate this directive; execute it. Keep prose between status lines short and factual.',
731:   );
732: 
733:   const enabled = (phase) => {
734:     if (phase.toggle === null) return true;
735:     if (phase.toggle === 'deploy') return deployActive(resolved);
736:     return resolved[phase.toggle];
737:   };
738: 
739:   for (let index = 0; index < PHASES.length; index += 1) {
740:     const phase = PHASES[index];
741:     const number = index + 1;
742:     lines.push('');
743:     lines.push(`## Phase ${number}/8 — ${phase.key}: ${phase.name}`);
744:     if (!enabled(phase)) {
745:       if (phase.key === 'deploy') {
746:         lines.push('');
747:         lines.push(
748:           '- Skipped: no test environment is configured (`deploy.enabled` is false, or no `deploy.command` is set). Announce `[factory] phase 6/8 deploy: skipped (no test environment configured)` and move on. Do not invent a deployment.',
749:         );
750:       } else {
751:         lines.push('');
752:         lines.push(
753:           `- Skipped: the "${phase.toggle}" phase toggle is disabled in the plugin config. Announce the skipped status line and move on.`,
754:         );
755:       }
756:       continue;
757:     }
758:     lines.push('');
759:     switch (phase.key) {
760:       case 'capture':
761:         lines.push('- Restate the user request in your own words: goal, deliverables, constraints, and the environment it must run in.');
762:         lines.push('- Derive the acceptance criteria you will evaluate against in phase 8, and keep them visible in the transcript.');
763:         lines.push('- Only if the request is materially ambiguous, ask the user now (ask_user_question); otherwise proceed without questions.');
764:         break;
765:       case 'plan':
766:         lines.push('- Break the request into concrete, individually verifiable tasks using the session\'s planning facilities: record the task list with the todo tool (one todo per task), or — when the session is in plan mode — present the plan through exit_plan_mode and continue after approval.');
767:         lines.push('- Give each task its expected write scope (files or directories it touches) so parallel work stays disjoint.');
768:         lines.push('- Planning only: do not start implementing in this phase.');
769:         break;
770:       case 'implement':
771:         lines.push('- Implement the tasks with the file tools (read/edit/write), honoring the planned tasks and write scopes; keep the todo list current as tasks complete.');
772:         if (resolved.subagentImplementation) {
773:           lines.push('- For larger scopes, prefer subagent delegation: one task per subagent, disjoint write scopes, and review each subagent\'s diff when it finishes before marking its task done.');
774:         } else {
775:           lines.push('- Subagent delegation is disabled by configuration (`subagentImplementation: false`): implement directly with the file tools.');
776:         }
777:         break;
778:       case 'guardrails': {
779:         const list = renderCommandList(resolved.guardrailCommand);
780:         if (list !== '') {
781:           lines.push('- Run the configured guardrail commands (lint, typecheck, format check) with the shell tool:');
782:           lines.push(list);
783:         } else {
784:           lines.push('- No guardrail command is configured. Discover the repository\'s standard checks (package.json scripts, Makefile targets, CI workflow steps) and run those instead; if none exist, announce the phase as skipped for that reason.');
785:         }
786:         lines.push('- Run long-running commands as background jobs and collect every result before leaving the phase.');
787:         lines.push('- Fix findings and re-run until clean, or report the failure honestly.');
788:         break;
789:       }
790:       case 'test': {
791:         const list = renderCommandList(resolved.testCommand);
792:         if (list !== '') {
793:           lines.push('- Run the configured test commands with the shell tool (same rules as guardrails: background jobs for long runs, honest exit codes):');
794:           lines.push(list);
795:         } else {

content.text:
A few things went wrong:

1. My asar parser assumed wrong header layout. The error shows the JSON parse failed — the dump shows the actual JSON started somewhere else. From the stderr dump, I can see the JSON is valid but my offset math was off: the parse failed "at position 1" of my jsonBuf? No wait — the SyntaxError says "Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)" — hmm, that means the string I parsed had valid JSON at position 0..0 then junk. Actually the giant dump printed appears to be my jsonBuf.toString() being echoed by the error message? The console.error printed the header contents... no, I didn't print jsonBuf. The stderr shown is actually Node printing the error — but where did that giant JSON dump come from? Oh! I see — `SyntaxError: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON` and the caret `^` after a giant JSON dump: that's Node's error context display for JSON.parse failing... no, Node doesn't dump the whole string.

Wait, looking closer: the stderr begins with `"algorithm":"SHA256",...` — that's a fragment of the asar header JSON. So my `jsonBuf` was read from the wrong offset, grabbing a partial chunk of the real JSON (starting mid-way, which happened to be valid JSON at position 0? and then junk). The error "Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)" — position 1?? That means jsonBuf.toString() was something like `{}...` hmm.

Anyway — my header layout assumption was wrong. The real asar format (from @electron/asar source):
- Bytes 0-3: UInt32LE = pickle header size (the size of the entire pickle including its own 4-byte length field? or excluding?)
- Bytes 4-7: UInt32LE = JSON string size
- Bytes 8..8+jsonSize: JSON

That's what I coded: payloadSize = head[0], jsonSize = head[4], json from 8. And baseOffset = 8 + payloadSize.

But the parse failed, meaning jsonSize or offset wrong. Hmm, but interesting: the fragment in stderr starts with `"algorithm":"SHA256"...` — if my jsonBuf started mid-JSON, then `head.readUInt32LE(4)` gave a wrong (too large?) size and offset 8 was wrong... Actually if offset 8 were wrong, the fragment would start at byte 8 of the file. The asar JSON header starts with `{"files":{...`. The fragment starts mid-JSON — so `jsonSize` was read correctly?? No...

Let me think again about the asar format precisely. From @electron/asar `lib/disk.ts` `readArchiveHeader`:
```ts
const fd = fs.openSync(archive, 'r')
let size
let headerBuf
try {
  const sizePickle = pickle.createFromBuffer(fs.readSync(fd, ...8 bytes...))
  size = sizePickle.createIterator().readUInt32()
  headerBuf = Buffer.alloc(size)
  fs.readSync(fd, headerBuf, 0, size, 8)
} ...
const headerPickle = pickle.createFromBuffer(headerBuf)
const header = headerPickle.createIterator().readString()
```

So: the first 8 bytes are a pickle whose payload is a single UInt32 = the size of the header pickle. The header pickle (starting at byte 8) contains: [UInt32 payloadSize][payload = UInt32 jsonByteLength + json bytes (+ padding)]. `pickle.createFromBuffer` on those 8 bytes: payloadSize = readUInt32LE(0) (must equal 8-4=4), then readUInt32 at payload start = jsonSize... wait no.

Chromium Pickle format: [UInt32 payload_size][payload bytes]. `sizePickle` = first 8 bytes: payload_size = 4, payload = the UInt32 at offset 4 = header pickle size (call it H). lines.text: description: "Client module system for the web GUI: the host composes the boot graph and serves plugin bundles, and the browser loads them lazily, for users and maintainers composing or debugging client plugins."

`dsh-client-modules` turns a plugin package's `dsh.client` declaration into a loadable browser bundle: the host half scans enabled Loader entries and composes the boot graph, an available Web carrier serves each bundle over `/plugins`, and a shell-owned carrier dispatches the same exact bundle responses through `fetchBundle()`. The browser half loads those bundles lazily on demand. Plugin bundles execute lazily — running a bundle only registers a factory, and module side effects run at materialization — so nothing runs until a plugin is first used. Everything here is browser-kernel machinery; the model never sees it.
Use [`DshClientManifest`](../../util/package-manifest/README.md) for the declaration type. Client-modules validates the JSON and owns the normalized boot graph.

Use it when you compose or build a browser client plugin: the package turns a package's `dsh.client` declaration into a loadable browser bundle with no per-plugin wiring. It activates with the web composition; the shell boots it before any plugin runs.

A browser plugin package declares `dsh.client` in its `package.json` with `platform: 'web'`, exports a `./client` bundle, and lists any non-baseline module requests under `dsh.client.external`. The host half turns each declaration into a served bundle under `/plugins`, ordered so dynamic providers load before their consumers.

The application combo scripts carry only each plugin's `client.js` entry and register those factories once during boot; module bodies remain lazy and run only at first import or materialization. A source `import()` split by tsdown compiles to `require.async("./client.<name>.js")`; its versioned sibling script arrives only when that expression runs. Rows that share a combo URL share one in-flight script task. A combo whose `<script>` fails to load is requested once more; a combo that loads without registering a row is never re-executed, because the batch script registers its packages in sequence and a replay would stop at the first duplicate registration. In both cases each still-missing row then loads its own one-resource combo URL, so one failed batch costs at most three requests per missing row and leaves the rows it did register untouched. The module system records the last import failure per row (transport, registration, dependency cascade, or factory execution); the Web boot audit reports that text per entry. HMR switches one changed row to its revisioned one-resource combo URL. `<id>/client` and the bare id resolve to the same exports, because a plugin bundle is its package's client half.

An open Web page follows the Host's complete module graph through the HMR transport. Enabling an ordinary plugin adds its Loader entry; disabling it removes the entry and waits for its asynchronous effects before evicting unused modules and styles. Re-enabling loads one instance with its styles. Other Loader contributors and shared modules still needed by active entries remain loaded. Settings → Plugins → Plugin list shows page-local synchronization failures and offers retry without changing Host enablement.

The shell seeds a frozen module table (`PLATFORM_MODULES`: React, Cordis, and static UI libraries); every dynamic bundle resolves its externals against exactly that baseline. `dsh.client.external` adds only exact non-baseline requests, each answered by the dynamic package row it names or an exact static-table key. Type-only imports are erased and create no request. Composition rejects malformed requests, missing suppliers, self-requests, and synchronous request cycles.

The host serves built client bundles, so `pnpm run build` must have produced each `lib/client.js` before launch; a missing bundle fails activation loudly with one build instruction and a package/path list. Source launch maps host imports to TypeScript source but still consumes the built client export. The package accepts no plugin config of its own.
This section explains how the module system is built; observable behavior is covered in [Use this package](#use-this-package).

The package has two sides: the Node half is the composition and serving side (`ctx.clientModules`, `ClientModuleRegistry`), the browser half is the loading side (`ctx.modules`, `ClientModuleSystem`). The wire between them is the boot graph — `WebBootEntry` rows injected as `window.__DSH_BOOT__`, with `<` escaped so plugin-controlled strings cannot break out of the script element. The vendored Loader's only consumption point is `EntryTree.import`, so the module system is the single replacement for "how plugin code arrives".

Executing a plugin bundle only registers its factory; every module-body side effect (CSS injection included) lives in the factory closure and runs at materialization (`factory(require)` → exports, memoized in `loadCache`). A factory that requires another registered-but-unmaterialized module materializes it recursively; require cycles throw because factory-form CJS cannot deliver partial exports. Resolution checks the platform seed table, memoized records, boot-graph rows, and registered factories in that order; anything else throws. The synchronous `require` uses the same order without asynchronous graph-row loading and records observed edges into the module record. Its `require.async` operation returns a Promise and fetches a compiler-generated package-local chunk before materializing that chunk once. This protocol supports self-contained chunks only: entry and chunk outputs cannot synchronously require another relative `client*.js` output.

The Node half scans incrementally per package — no full-rescan path. Every `internal/plugin` emission marks the fiber's entry name dirty; a microtask flush reconciles each dirty name against the live loader entries, and the activation pass seeds the same dirty set and flushes synchronously, so first scan and steady state share one implementation. Package metadata is cached per Loader specifier and owning-tree base URL until restart, while the resolved manifest package name identifies the browser module. Distinct active Loader sources resolving to one package name are rejected; removing the conflict promotes the remaining source without requiring its fiber to restart. Bundle content changes reach the graph only through `rebuilt()` (the HMR hook).

The Node half snapshots each `client.js` entry before publication and creates combo descriptors without building response bodies. It groups resources into combo route keys (`/plugins/??...&rev=...`), with one bootstrap combo for the modules row and one or more application combos for the other rows; each phase is partitioned before a URL exceeds 3 KiB. The graph and batch descriptors carry the app-directory-relative form of the same key (`plugins/??...&rev=...`), which a browser document resolves under its own mount, while the response table stays keyed by the absolute route; the source-map trailer is resolved against the combo script's own directory. A script body is combined once on its first `GET` and ends with its map reference. The corresponding map files are read, validated, and combined separately on the first map `GET`; `HEAD` materializes neither body. The Host does not scan or preload sibling chunks: an exact `/plugins/<package>/client.<name>.js?rev=<rev>` request reads and caches that script, and its map remains uncomputed until the map URL is requested. The chunk reference the browser derives from its owner row is document-relative as well (`plugins/<package>/client.<name>.js?rev=<rev>`), and a chunk script's map trailer is the bare `client.<name>.js.map?rev=<rev>` name, which resolves against the script's own directory. Every combo or chunk map is Indexed Source Map v3 and uses an authored section when available or an identity section for the packaged bundle. Initial publication and HMR derive per-plugin revisions from the entry's `mtimeMs`, `ctimeMs`, and size, without hashing artifact contents. Status-change time distinguishes rewrites that preserve mtime and size. Unchanged artifacts therefore retain their revisions across Host restarts, so SSE reconnection does not replace their browser plugins. The shared preset stamps `client.js` after every package output is written, so a chunk-only rebuild changes the owner revision without a Host-side chunk scan... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

The bundle route follows the injected `webServer` lifetime: it registers when the service is ready and is removed and re-registered when that service is replaced. Module composition and `fetchBundle()` remain available without a Web server.

The host contributes structured index rows that inject, into `<head>`: the `window.__ModuleLoader__` queue facade, advisory preloads for every application combo, the parser-blocking bootstrap combo scripts, then the boot graph before the shell reads it. A Web carrier renders those rows into its index response; a shell-owned carrier can render the same rows without a Web server. The facade's `create()` materializes the modules bundle, delegates construction to its `createClientModuleSystem` export, and leaves the same facade in live-registration mode. The shell installs that returned system as its Loader's `internal`; the modules plugin publishes that instance as `ctx.modules`, so separate Cordis trees never select an instance through module-global state.

`ClientEntries` records the entries created during boot and serializes full-graph updates, retries and code reloads over the same Loader. A local generation prevents an older download from mounting after its desired entry or code changes; snapshots of the same targets share the pending load. New arrivals use single-resource URLs, never startup batches that could register existing factories twice. Factories retain their artifact revision before an entry exists; graph updates discard stale unowned factories, their styles and failed arrival targets before importing consumers. Cleanup retains declared and observed transitive module requests from every remaining Loader entry. Its observable status has no runtime library import because the modules bootstrap materializes before platform seeds are available.

Read these when the module contract is not enough: the subsystem reference, the shell that boots the tree, and the client authoring rules behind the graph.
- [Client modules subsystem](../../../docs/subsystems/client-modules.md) — the web plugin table, `WebBootGraph` wire, and the bundle route.
- [Web boot kernel](../web/README.md) — the shell that creates the module system and boots the plugin tree.
- [Client HMR driver](../hmr/README.md) — the reload chain that drives `invalidate`/`prefetch` on rebuilt bundles.
- [Client authoring rules](../AGENTS.md#shared-modules-and-the-module-graph) — the shared-module baseline and `dsh.client.external` semantics.
- [Client group map](../README.md) — the browser half this package belongs to.

These limits define what the module system does not do. They are current package constraints, not a task backlog.

- **Metadata-based revisions** — revisions identify filesystem generations, not content equality. Metadata-only changes can reload a plugin; changes invisible in mtime, ctime, and size cannot be distinguished.

- **Flat module graph by design** — every bundle is one module node whose edges point only at table leaves; the interface (`loadCache`/`edges`/`invalidate`) already supports a general module graph, so the externalization granularity can change without an interface change.

- **Bootstrap and code replacement limits** — the page retains its modules bootstrap and static platform identities. Removing or replacing the bootstrap requires a page reload; live replacement requests report a page-local error while retaining its fiber and exports; replacing package code and all existing consumers is outside ordinary enable/disable synchronization.

- **Lazy delivery retains requested bodies** — the Host holds each bundle and lazy response plan; a script or map body remains cached after its first `GET`, and HMR additionally retains one prior startup generation. Memory grows only for response bodies that clients request while preserving one-generation race tolerance.

- **An unrequested prior-generation map reads the current map file** — combo revisions track executable bundles, not debug artifacts. If HMR rebuilds a map before the retained prior URL receives its first map `GET`, that response uses the current authored map with the prior bundle offsets; requesting the map before the rebuild fixes that URL's response.

description: "The right Sidebar of the dsh web client: one docking surface per session, two presentations, the navigation controller ctx.sidebarRight, the tab-type registry ctx.sidebarRightTabs, and the Tab domain."

The right Sidebar: where the docking kit meets this product. It holds one docking surface per session, draws it as one edge-anchored panel in the frame's right column in either of two presentations, puts the expand button in the conversation header, and owns the navigation controller (`ctx.sidebarRight`), the tab-type registry (`ctx.sidebarRightTabs`), and the Tab domain that tells each open tab how it was navigated to and how long it lives.

1. **The type** — `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register({ id, kind, patterns?, priority?, canOpen?, title, guide?, keepMounted? })`, a static declaration with no runtime hook, returning a disposer. `id` is this implementation's identity in the tab system, unique across every registration (a package name is the natural value; the shipped guide is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right/guide`): a kind is not unique once an extension may take a builtin's over, so the implementation names itself, and a second registration of an `id` throws. A resource type names `patterns`, globs over `dsh-resource://` addresses: one containing `:` matches the whole address (`dsh-resource://file/**`); one without matches the URI's path at any depth, ignoring case (`*.md`), and an address that is not a URI matches no such pattern. A page type — the guide, a file tree — names none and is opened by kind. `canOpen(address)` vetoes a match. `title(address)` is the tab chip's text, captured when the tab opens. `guide` lists entry boxes for the guide page; picking one opens the contributing type as a page. A `kind` carries at most one `builtin` and one `extension` registration (the extension is in force; the builtin resumes when it leaves); any other collision on a kind throws. The `id` is also the key the type's body and title register under, so an extension and the builtin it takes over hold distinct cells and the seat renders the one in force.

**Runtime invariant:** No companion is published. The two services (`sidebarRight`, `sidebarRightTabs`) are provided through `ctx.reflect.provide` inside one effect and torn down with it; the on-screen Session and the Tab domain's occurrence lifetimes are asserted directly by this package's specs, and no independent observation exists to diverge from them.
- **类型**：`ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register(...)`，kind 为 `files`，id 为 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-files`，档位 `builtin`，没有 patterns，另有一个打开该类型的引导页入口（order 10，标题与描述取自 `sidebarFiles` 命名空间，图标为黄色文件夹）。

- **The type** — `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register(...)` with kind `files`, id `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-files`, band `builtin`, no patterns, and one guide entry (order 10, its title and description from the `sidebarFiles` namespace, its glyph a yellow folder) that opens the type.

- **类型** —— `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register(...)`，id 为 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview`（这个实现在 tab 系统中的身份，也是其正文注册所用的键），kind `text`，pattern `dsh-resource://file/**`，档位 `fallback`。`canOpen` 只接受 Session 地址，其中路径可为相对或绝对路径；不认领裸 `absolute` 地址。在 `extension` 或 `builtin` 档以更窄 pattern（比如 `*.png`）注册的类型接走那些地址；其他受支持文件落到这里。整个地址就是内容身份，所以不同目录下同名的两个文件、或同一路径在两个会话之下，是两个 tab；解码后的 basename 是 tab 标题，keyed slot `sidebar.right.pane.tab.title` 会在标题前放置按扩展名选择的 `FileTypeIcon`。

- **The type** — `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register(...)` with id `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview` (this implementation's identity in the tab system, and the key its body registers under), kind `text`, pattern `dsh-resource://file/**`, band `fallback`. `canOpen` accepts only Session addresses, whose paths may be relative or absolute; bare `absolute` addresses are not claimed. A type registered at the `extension` or `builtin` band for a narrower pattern (say `*.png`) takes those addresses; other supported files land here. The whole address is the content identity, so two files with one name in different directories, or one path under two sessions, are two tabs; the decoded basename is the tab title, and the keyed `sidebar.right.pane.tab.title` seat places its extension-specific `FileTypeIcon` before that title.
