Reload restores that layout before tab bodies render; switching Sessions keeps their layouts independent. Providers restore their own content from the retained tab identity and resource address, including [terminal reconnection](../ui-sidebar-terminal/README.md#use-this-package). Navigation parameters, resource contents and live connections are not layout state. Undo history stays in memory and resets on reload. Saved field types, node membership, selection, identity counters and the one-pane or two-horizontal-pane dock layout are validated before adoption or startup discovery; invalid data clears only its Session key. Storage failures leave the current layout usable in memory. Windows at the same origin share the last saved layout per Session; each active window keeps its own current layout until reload.

`sidebarRight.openTabs` publishes stable metadata for every open tab across saved and adopted Sessions. Startup discovery reads the layout keys without mounting dormant content, pinning files or activating Agents. Adopted stores replace their own metadata on membership commits, and permanently cleared scopes remove it. Other windows' storage writes do not overwrite this window's live membership. Providers use this inventory to restore their own resource lifetimes.

A tab type registers in two stages, and the shipped guide type goes through exactly the same public path a type from another package does (`ui-sidebar-documentpreview` is the live proof). Both stages sit inside the type's own `ctx.effect`, so the registration lives exactly as long as the plugin that made it.

1. **The type** — `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register({ id, kind, patterns?, priority?, canOpen?, title, guide?, keepMounted? })`, a static declaration with no runtime hook, returning a disposer. `id` is this implementation's identity in the tab system, unique across every registration (a package name is the natural value; the shipped guide is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right/guide`): a kind is not unique once an extension may take a builtin's over, so the implementation names itself, and a second registration of an `id` throws. A resource type names `patterns`, globs over `dsh-resource://` addresses: one containing `:` matches the whole address (`dsh-resource://file/**`); one without matches the URI's path at any depth, ignoring case (`*.md`), and an address that is not a URI matches no such pattern. A page type — the guide, a file tree — names none and is opened by kind. `canOpen(address)` vetoes a match. `title(address)` is the tab chip's text, captured when the tab opens. `guide` lists entry boxes for the guide page; picking one opens the contributing type as a page. A `kind` carries at most one `builtin` and one `extension` registration (the extension is in force; the builtin resumes when it leaves); any other collision on a kind throws. The `id` is also the key the type's body and title register under, so an extension and the builtin it takes over hold distinct cells and the seat renders the one in force.

2. **The body** — `ctx.slots.register({ name: 'sidebar.right.pane.tab', key: definition.id }, Body)` reads `{ sidebar, panel, tab }` through the framework-injected `useTabInfo()`. `sidebar` supplies expansion and fullscreen information; `panel.id` identifies its pane; `tab` contains the record fields, `visible`, `navigation`, `signal`, and `actions`. These are not parallel owner props; the type's own store still uses `useStore`/`actions`. Optional title registrations and guide replacements share this hook; an absent title registration uses the text captured at open time. The title wrapper retains tab and occurrence DOM markers without adding a layout box, so dockkit controls icon spacing and vertical alignment in docked tabs and floating headers.

Which type opens a resource follows the editor-resolver convention: the types whose `patterns` match are ranked by `priority` band — `extension` (a type from outside the product, the highest, and the default when none is named), `builtin`, `fallback` (plain viewers anything more specific should beat) — then by the length of the matched pattern, then by registration order; `canOpen` removes a candidate. The bands are string literals so a type in another package needs no runtime import from here. `candidates(address)` returns the ranking, `claim(address, kind?)` the decision; naming a `kind` skips its globs but keeps its `canOpen`.

Two more seats extend what is already there: `sidebar.right.tab.guide` (chain) replaces the guide tab's body without replacing the tab, and `sidebar.right.tab.menu.item` (list) appends content-level actions to a tab's menu after the kit's own layout actions. No seat exists for pane-level actions or for collapsed-state controls yet, because nothing needs one.

`openResource(address, options?)` and `openTab(kind, options?)` are the navigation controller, and every way into the column calls one of them: the conversation's file links and a tool row's line reference (`openResource(fileAddress, { params: { line } })`), the strip's add control and a guide entry box (`openTab`), a file tree's rows (`tab.actions.openResource`). A resource address is a `dsh-resource://<type>/…` URI; without `options.kind` the registry claims it (globs and `canOpen`, best band wins), with it that kind's type in force opens it. A page is named by kind; the tab is recorded under an address this package composes and nobody else spells (`contract/seed.ts`). Both run the same steps as one history entry: a resource tab already showing the same (kind, contentId) is focused wherever it sits unless `revealIfOpened: false`; ordinary page tabs always deduplicate within the target pane, regardless of that option; otherwise a new tab lands in `options.replaceTab`'s pane and slot (closing that tab), else `options.paneId`, else the active docked pane; the panel expands, because content the user cannot see is not opened. Then the Tab domain records the navigation — `params` reach the body as `navigation.params`, with `revision` stepped — outside the layout history. `params` is typed by what is opened: a viewer for a resource type merges its entry into `SidebarRightResourceParamsMap` (the text preview declares `{ line?: number }`); a page type that takes parameters merges into `SidebarRightTabParamsMap` under its kind; values are JSON-shaped by convention, unchecked at run time. An address outside `dsh-resource://`, one no type claims, or a kind nothing registered throws: that is a wiring mistake, not a user error.

`close(tabId)` closes a tab; `active()` reads the active tab. `isExpanded()` and `toggleExpanded()` read and drive the column's expansion; `toggleFullscreen(target)` applies the panel control’s display-mode action to a captured dock pane. Layout operations, for callers that arrange the column programmatically, each recorded like the gesture it stands in for: `focus(tabId)` focuses a tab and its pane; `split(paneId?)` splits a docked pane (the active one by default) under the same pane budget and room rule as the strip's control and returns the new pane's id, or `undefined` — recording nothing — when it cannot; `float(tabId, rect?)` takes a docked tab out into a panel; `dock(paneId)` returns a floating panel to the active docked pane. A tab or pane that does not exist, or already is where the call would put it, is left alone. The face exposes operations only: no layout snapshot, no operation log, no lookup by address. `_undo()` / `_redo()` step the on-screen surface's history; they are `@internal` — the sequence has no user-facing control, and these exist for tests. Commands act on the on-screen Session through its adopted store; with no Session on screen, or before the runtime mints its store, they throw rather than write into a surface nobody draws. `mounted` is the observable of the Session on screen: the selected Session while the Conversation fills the main column, `undefined` while a global panel replaces it or no Session is selected. The plugin derives it from the Session selection and `ctx.layout.panelInfo`, and it changes before React renders the change that causes it, so a component rendered in that commit reads the arriving Session and may act on it from its effects: the frame renders that Session's seat in the same pass, which mints its store. Seats never publish it; each reports only what it renders with: the room its docking kit measured, which `split` and `preferNewPane` apply to that Session's panes (unmeasured panes have room), and whether it (line truncated)

`focusedTarget(element?)` resolves the current DOM pane and tab, including an embedding iframe; outside focus returns no page. `commandTarget(element?)` additionally allows an outside open to use the on-screen Session's active dock pane. Captures include the occurrence and navigation revision; `isTargetCurrent(target)` rejects changed Sessions, moved or reopened tabs, and intervening navigation. Focus and pointer activation remain separate from persisted layout selection.

The Tab domain retains a branded occurrence id, navigation, an abort signal, and bound actions per (Session, tab id). A private assembly callback adopts each Session's store, reconciles restored records immediately, and follows its commits. Reconstructing a Session store replaces its adoption, releasing the old subscription and cleanup reference. Only record removal or plugin unload aborts the signal; closing the sidebar and switching Sessions retain records, while undo restores a new occurrence. `useTabInfo()` composes framework-bound store and navigation hooks without manual component subscriptions or render-time record creation. `tab.actions` always target their own Session; `tab.visible` distinguishes bodies from titles and excludes background Sessions; foreground floating tabs remain visible when the sidebar closes. `adopt` is absent from the public controller.

A type's `keepMounted: true` retains visited bodies across tab and Session changes, collapse, and docking. Each View supplies its stable hold callback through owner props, so rebuilding Session injection bindings does not release a body. Unvisited bodies are not mounted eagerly.

Tab owners register `registerCloseHandler(kind, handler)` through an effect. A handler synchronously retains any background cleanup before allowing explicit close or replacement. The resource owner tracks completion and retry; the sidebar does not wait. A thrown handler preserves the tab. Collapse, presentation changes and plugin disposal do not invoke close handlers; the tab abort signal identifies occurrence disposal, not an explicit close.

Close and refresh commands resolve the focused pane and tab occurrence. Page bodies bind their refresh operation through `tab.actions.bindCommands()` and release it on unmount; ended occurrences cannot regain capabilities. Refresh never reloads the application. Shortcut page opens, sidebar expansion, and all splits focus the selected dock or floating pane after its DOM commits, including singleton reveals and guide replacements. Sidebar expansion focuses the active dock pane; collapse preserves focus inside floating panes. Pane focus preserves existing text selections. If a focused page input or iframe is replaced, focus returns to its visible pane only while no other element owns focus; an outside pointer gesture or explicit blur cancels this restoration. Close checks the captured identity again and uses resource cleanup. After a keyboard or native-menu close, focus moves to a surviving visible pane in the same Session so consecutive close commands continue there. Stale targets and cleanup failures never fall back to closing a window. Modal restrictions follow the [shortcut service](../shortcuts/README.md). The close command first requests the foreground modal’s close action; a modal that declines dismissal, a menu, or an unregistered dialog blocks closing the sidebar or window behind it. Closing the sole docked guide with a shortcut or native menu collapses the sidebar and retains the guide. Desktop requests window closure through the shortcut service only when no modal is open and no sidebar page owns focus; Web leaves the browser open.

Each `guide` entry has an `id` unique within its provider. The guide renders `sidebar.right.tab.guide.entry` by the active definition id, forwarding the entry id, resolved title and optional description, plus the framework `useTabInfo` hook. A provider can register a custom card under its definition id; otherwise the standard icon/title button renders. The sidebar owns width and placement, while custom components own their markup and interaction. Guide cards use the shared R20 radius, including hover fills and provider-owned split buttons. Entry identity remains stable across sorting and unrelated registrations. Unboxed shortcut text aligns at the right. The terminal shell menu sits beside its entry title.

A tab type can declare `multiple: true` for independent instances such as terminals. Each open receives a distinct content address, so placement and docking preserve those instances; ordinary pages retain per-pane uniqueness.

Default pages depend on the number of registered guide entries, not the number of tab types or open tabs. Exactly one entry opens its page directly; zero or multiple entries open the guide. Explicitly adding a guide still opens the guide, even with one entry. The sole docked guide is the only tab that cannot close; closing any other sole tab also collapses the column. The chip, context menu, and `close` API apply the same rule.

The guide tab is a muted compass over one entry capsule per `guide` entry the registered types contributed, in `order`, centred in the body; the guide has no words of its own. A capsule shows the entry's glyph — or the guide's quieter cube placeholder when the entry registered none — and its title; while at most four entries are listed, an entry that registered a `description` shows it under the title, and a longer list drops every description. Picking a default capsule calls `tab.actions.openTab(entry.kind, { replaceTab: true })`, so the guide gives way to the page it opened. A pane holds at most one guide tab. The strip's add control is drawn only while its pane holds none and opens one there with `openTab('guide', { paneId, revealIfOpened: false })`, so a guide in another pane does not capture the click; opening the guide into a pane that already has one focuses it instead; a guide dragged, dropped, or docked into such a pane merges into it — the arriving guide closes and the pane's own is focused; `duplicateTab` on the guide records nothing. A split, an expanded empty root pane, and the pane a sole tab vacates by dropping on its own edge use the same default-page rule, one tab per new pane; the self-edge drop leaves the dragged tab focused. A plain `openTab('guide')` opens or focuses the guide only within the active or named pane. Splitting an empty pane does nothing and returns no new pane. The product allows two horizontal panes, initially equal, with divider ratios limited to 20%–80%. Insufficient width blocks a new split; with two panes already present, a body drop moves the tab between panes instead of creating a third. At the two-pane limit, split controls are disabled with a focusable reason; closing back to one pane enables them.

Every string in the column comes from the `sidebarRight` locale namespace, including the kit's accessible names. A tab's title is fixed when the tab is minted; a type's display name follows the current language.
None, as the package is a browser-side UI plugin layer that registers nothing model-facing.
- **Retained Session deletion.** Catalog absence alone does not retire an initialized retained View; its tab lifetimes and plugin teardown own release.

The projection read path is confirmed: `ctx.sessions.binding(sessionId).session.projections.faceOf(key)` — exactly what our client.js does (with optional chaining). Good — that part is correct in principle.

Now, the critical remaining questions:

1. **How are occupant `inject()` results delivered as props?** From dsh-client-ui-session line 127: `keyedHooks: { projection: (key) => ... }`. Interesting — there are `keyedHooks` too. And from plan: `inject: (sessionId) => ({ ...open(sessionId), keyedHooks: {...} })` — the inject callback **receives the dispatch key as argument** (for keyed slots, the key; for session slots, the sessionId?). And in jobs: `inject: () => ({ hooks: {...}, watchRows, observe, killJob })`.

So how do `hooks` become `use<Key>` props? Need to see the slot system's occupant rendering. The `hooks: { jobs: ... }` → prop `useJobs`? Our plugin assumes `hooks: { factoryState: (standard) => () => useFactoryView(...) }` becomes prop `useFactoryState`. Note ours has an extra layer: `factoryState: (standard) => () => ...` — a function taking `standard` and returning a hook. Why? The client.js comment says "Hook factories receive `(standard, context)`; `standard.sessionId` identifies the session whose projection the tab reads."

Hmm — that looks wrong. In plan, `inject: (sessionId) => ...` receives the sessionId directly. In our client.js, `inject: () => ({ t, hooks: { factoryState: (standard) => () => ... } })`. If the framework calls occupant `inject(dispatchKey)` and spreads the result as props (converting `hooks.x` → `useX`), then our `factoryState` prop would be `(standard) => () => ...` — a function, NOT a hook — and `FactoryTabBody` destructures `useFactoryState` and calls `useFactoryState()`. Wait — destructured name is `useFactoryState`. If props are `{ t, useFactoryState: (standard) => () => ... }`, then `useFactoryState()` calls the outer function with no args → returns `() => useFactoryView(...)` — a function, not a view. Then `view` = that function → `view === undefined`? No — it's a function, so `view.phases` undefined → renders phases = [] → started = view.running (undefined) || some(...) → false → empty state "No active factory run". So the tab might render but never shows progress. That's a plausible bug #1 in client.js. Need to verify how hooks are passed: maybe `hooks.x` is called with something by the framework. Let me look at the slot system (dsh-client-ui-slots) to get the exact occupant contract: `inject` result → props mapping, `hooks` → `use<Key>`, `keyedHooks` → ? and how the dispatch key flows.

2. **What `standard`/`context` do hook factories receive?** Our comment claims `(standard, context)` with `standard.sessionId`. Plan uses `inject: (sessionId) => ...`. Goal uses `hooks`/`keyedHooks` differently. Let me read dsh-client-ui-slots sources (lib/client.js + README).

3. **The tab type registration `priority: 'extension'`** — valid ('extension' band exists). But `kind: 'factory'` with no `patterns` → a page type opened by kind — fine. But how does the user open it? A page type without a guide entry is openable only via `openTab('factory')` — nothing calls that! The shipped page types either have `guide` entries (so they appear in the guide picker / default page) or are opened programmatically. Our plugin registers no `guide` entry, so the tab can NEVER be opened by the user. Hmm — "doesn't work at all" might partly be this! With `guide: [{ id, kind, title, ... }]` the tab type contributes an entry box to the guide page, and with exactly one entry registered across all types, "Exactly one entry opens its page directly" — but shipped types already register guide entries (files order 10, terminal probably, etc.), so ours would be one among many — the guide shows it as a capsule. That's the sanctioned way to make the tab reachable. 

4. **`sessions` inject**: our inject list includes `sessions` — fine.

5. **`locale` service**: `ctx.locale.register(NS, {zh, en})` + `bind` — matches jobs/plan. Good. And registration `locale: NS` in slot register — plan does that too (`locale: NS`).

6. **Host half**: need to verify `sessionProjections.register` definition contract — exact field names (`key`, `stateVersion`, `stateSchema`, `init`, `apply`, `wire.view`, `wire.viewSchema`), the event shape (`event.type === 'assistant/message'`, `event.data.message.content`), and whether a dynamic (non-predeclared) key like 'factory' is allowed (second overload suggests yes: `Exclude<keyof SessionProjectionStateMap, keyof SessionProjectionMap>` — keys with state but no built-in wire? Hmm, actually need to read the real dsh-session-projection package to see `ProjectionDefinition`). Also `stateVersion` might be `version`? Let me read the session-projection package.

Also how does the wire view reach the client — via `dsh-api-session-controller` client `sessions` binding — `session.projections.faceOf(key)` returns `ObservableSnapshot<unknown>`. The projection snapshot for a session gets computed by host `sessionProjections.snapshot(session)` → includes wire views of registered projections? Need to check how snapshot flows: `refreshProjections(sessionId)` exists on client sessions service. Fine.

7. **The event type**: is it really `assistant/message` with `event.data.message.content`? Need to check the SessionEvent shape in dsh-session. Let me grep.

Also check what shipped projections do for `wire`: e.g. `inbox`, `modelSelection`, `plan`, `goal` — find their registration definitions in host packages (dsh-session, dsh-goal, dsh-plan-mode). The `goal` one is a great reference. Let me grep for `stateVersion` across the tree.

Let me check the slots package and the session-projection package.

This is the definitive pattern for a projection-fed occupant (goal):

```js
inject: (sessionId) => {
    const binding = sessions.binding(sessionId);
    if (binding === void 0) throw new Error(...);
    return {
        hooks: { goalActivation: createGoalActivationSource({ projection: binding.session.projections.faceOf("goal"), ... }) },
        onEdit: ...,
    };
}
```

- `inject(sessionId)` — first arg is the sessionId. ✓
- `hooks: { goalActivation: source }` — the source is an OBSERVABLE (`createGoalActivationSource` builds `{subscribe, getSnapshot}`), consumed as `useGoalActivation(...)` prop. ✓

So our client.js must change `inject: () => ({ t, hooks: { factoryState: (standard) => () => ... } })` to `inject: (sessionId) => ({ t, hooks: { factoryState: <observable> } })` where the observable is the projection face itself (`binding.session.projections.faceOf('factory')`), or an absent-fallback observable when the projection/binding is missing.

Then in the component, `useFactoryState()` — the selector hook: `useSelector(sel, eq)` with `sel` undefined → `useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector(subscribe, getSnapshot, undefined, undefined, undefined)`. Does uSES-with-selector handle undefined selector? From the keyedObservableHook code: `observableHook(source)(selector ?? identity, comparison)` — they explicitly default the selector to identity when undefined. But bare `hook()` with no args would pass `sel = undefined` directly into `useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector`... The official `useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector` requires a selector. If undefined, it would crash when called (`selector(snapshot)` → TypeError). So components must call `useFactoryState()` with... hmm, shipped components call e.g. `useShortcuts((entries) => entries.find(...))` — always with a selector. And `useStore((state) => ...)`.

So our body should call `useFactoryState((view) => view)` or with a selecting function. Safest: `const view = useFactoryState((snapshot) => snapshot);`. If snapshot undefined (absent projection) → view undefined → empty state. 

Let me double check `useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector` with selector undefined — in the production build it does `selector(getSnapshot())`. `undefined(...)` → TypeError. So yes, must pass a selector. I'll use identity.

Now, does the component also get `sessionId` as a plain prop? ExpandButton received `sessionId` — that's the session standard kit plain props: `{...binding.props}` — the session binding's props probably include `sessionId`. Our component doesn't need it if inject closes over sessionId.

Now the remaining verification list for the client half:
1. `exports.inject` must list services that exist: `sidebarRightTabs` (exists when sidebar-right loaded — provided via ctx.reflect.provide by sidebar-right), `slots`, `locale`, `sessions` — all real. But note: shipped plugins like plan list `sidebarRight` and `sidebarRightTabs`. Ours lists `sidebarRightTabs` — fine. BUT the client Service inspect catalog earlier did NOT list `sidebarRightTabs`/`sidebarRight` — because that catalog probably only enumerates Typert-registered services. Whatever — the runtime service exists (reflect.provide). Since the web shell always composes sidebar-right (it's part of the base composition? or is it an optional plugin?). Hmm — is `dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right` always loaded? The GUI has a right sidebar (the user sees tabs). The `dsh.client.inject` manifest of our plugin lists `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right` as a dependency — "ordered so dynamic providers load before their consumers" — good: it ensures sidebar-right's bundle loads before ours, so `sidebarRightTabs` exists when our entry activates.

2. Our tab type id: `@local/dsh-software-factory/factory-tab`. Fine (package name is natural value; subpath ids allowed — guide is `.../guide`).

3. `kind: 'factory'` — open via guide capsule (`openTab('factory')`). Add a `guide` entry so the user can discover/open it: `{ id: 'factory', order: 20, title: () => t('tab.title'), description: () => t('guide.description') }`. Need `icon`? Optional. We have our own glyph (FactoryGlyph) but guide icon must be a component (GuideArtworkFiles is a primitive component). We can pass our FactoryGlyph? "the guide's quieter cube placeholder when the entry registered none" — icon is a Component. Our FactoryGlyph is a function component — usable. But cautious: EntryBox may render icon at fixed size; ours takes `size` prop default 16. GuideArtwork* primitives are probably specialized. Simplest: omit `icon` (cube placeholder) or pass our glyph. I'll pass our glyph — it's a plain SVG component; EntryBox presumably renders `<entry.icon />` or with props. Risk: if EntryBox passes props like `className` — our component accepts `className`? FactoryGlyph({size=16, className}) — accepts className, fine.

Actually, let me check how EntryBox renders `entry.icon`. Grep EntryBox in sidebar-right.

Our FactoryTabTitle destructures `useTabInfo` — correct. But do we even need a custom title? "an absent title registration uses the text captured at open time" — the type's `title()` is captured when the tab opens. A custom title chip with the glyph is nice; keep it but make it minimal. Actually — the title wrapper must "retain tab and occurrence DOM markers" — shipped title components get `useTabInfo` too and must render... hmm, dockkit controls spacing. The guide's GuideTitle — let me look at what it renders. If title components need specific markers (DOM markers), maybe simplest is to NOT register a title and let the captured `title()` text serve. That's supported: "Optional title registrations". The chip then shows text only. Given "keep it simple and robust", I might drop the custom title registration. But the glyph in the chip is nice... Let me check GuideTitle quickly.

5. CSS: the shipped pattern matches ours (style tag with data-plugin-css). Ours is fine. Though there's a `styles.insert(css)` builtin for package-owned styles — the ModuleLoader `styles` builtin. Shipped built bundles do the manual tag (because they bundle CSS modules). Keep ours.

6. **Missing piece — `keepMounted`**: not needed.

7. What about opening the tab when /factory starts? Nice-to-have: when the run starts, open the tab automatically via `ctx.sidebarRight.openTab('factory')`. That would make the UI obviously "work". The plan plugin opens via openResource on user action. Auto-opening on projection change could annoy. But for discoverability the guide entry suffices... Hmm — but the user's complaint: "UI to show the factory running progress... doesn't work at all". The minimal fix: make the tab render correctly. Auto-open: I'd add it only on run start? That requires watching projections per session — heavier. Let me not auto-open; guide entry + correct rendering is the shipped-pattern way. Actually — wait. Let me reconsider: with a guide entry, the guide page lists a capsule; picking it opens the factory tab. Also "Exactly one entry opens its page directly" — there are already multiple entries (files, terminal...), so the guide shows. That's acceptable and standard.

Hmm, but actually — is auto-open warranted? The schedule/terminal don't auto-open. Standard UX: user opens the Factory tab from the guide; it then shows live progress. I'll mention it in README.

   b. Command definition fields: `{ name, description, input: { hint, attachments }, recordInput, handler }` — verify against dsh-commands.
   c. `agent.steer` — verify existence/shape.
   d. Whether the running host actually has this plugin loaded and the projection registered — I can't easily verify without the client page. But the fix is about code correctness; the user reinstalls+restarts (per AGENTS.md, reinstall happens from the settings repo session by Lead/user; and the running Host keeps old module generation until restart).

matches.line: 处理器返回 `success` 或 `error`，并可附带由适配器渲染的 UI 文本。`recordInput` 默认为 true；若载荷由命令自己的权威领域事件持有，命令会将 `recordInput` 设为 false，避免会话日志重复记录该输入。同一作用域内重复注册同名命令会抛出异常。
命令行的第 0 字节必须是斜杠，随后是小写名称（可含字母、数字、`_` 或 `-`），再之后是输入末尾或空白。名称之后的每个字节——包括分隔空白——都是该命令的 `rawInput`，命令自己拥有其专属语法。不符合命令语法、或名称未知的行会被适配器拒绝，而不是变成模型提示词。

命令可以声明 `input.attachments` 以接受 composer 图片与通用文件。执行器负责强制执行声明：把附件发给未声明的命令、附件存储缺失、会话范围内的文件上传凭证未知或图片批量超出限制，都会在处理器运行前以错误结果结算。图片以 base64 输入通过命令 wire，通用文件则引用后台上传完成后得到的凭证，因此命令提交不会再次读取文件字节。通过准入的 `ImageBlock` 与 `FileBlock` 按用户选择顺序组成冻结的 `invocation.attachments` 数组，其模型可见用途由处理器负责。

`dsh-commands` lets users run `/command [input]` actions in interactive Harness UIs without turning the command or its result into a model message. Commands can advertise input hints, accept attachments, and target one agent while preserving a global command with the same name for other agents. Every admitted run is recorded in the receiving agent's session log, while the UI renders the settled result outside model history. Use it for direct human controls in the `dsh` CLI or Web client; UI-less demos and ACP automation do not provide this command surface.

A plugin registers a command with `ctx.commands.register()`: a lowercase name, a discovery description, an optional `input` hint, and a handler. An optional branded `definitionId` gives the definition a stable, plugin-namespaced identity for adapters; it is independent of display copy and execution `commandId`. The effective descriptor carries only the selected definition's identity, so a scoped override never inherits the shadowed registration's identity.

The handler returns `success` or `error` plus optional UI text that the adapter renders. `recordInput` defaults to true; a command whose own authoritative domain event already carries the payload sets it to false so the session log does not duplicate the input. Registering the same name twice in one scope throws.

A command line starts with a slash at byte zero, a lowercase name containing letters, digits, `_` or `-`, and then either end-of-input or whitespace. Everything after the name — including separator whitespace — is the command's `rawInput`, and the command owns its own grammar for it. Lines that are not syntactically a command, or that name an unknown command, are rejected by the adapter instead of becoming a model prompt.

A command may declare `input.attachments` to accept composer images and generic files. The executor enforces the declaration: attachments sent to a non-declaring command, an absent attachment store, an unknown Session-scoped file-upload receipt, or an over-limit image batch each settle as an error before the handler runs. Images cross the command wire as base64 input; generic files cite receipts from their completed background uploads, so command submission never reads their bytes again. Admitted `ImageBlock`s and `FileBlock`s reach the handler as one frozen `invocation.attachments` array in the user's selection order, and the handler owns their model-visible use.

An interactive adapter calls `execute(agent, line, attachments, signal)` with the exact receiving agent, the full command line, and the submission's ordered attachments. It returns the settled `CommandExecution` — the normalized result plus its lifecycle `commandId` — or `undefined` for invalid syntax or an unknown name. `list(agent)` and `find(agent, name)` serve discovery after agent-scoped shadowing.

The registry itself submits nothing. Known slash commands execute in the UI command plane, and their `CommandResult` text is not submitted as a user message. Unknown slash-command input is rejected by shipped adapters instead of becoming a model prompt. A command producer may explicitly use the receiving `Agent`; for example, [`dsh-plan-mode`](../../plan/plan-mode/README.md#model-and-human-interactions) submits the optional message and ordered attachments in `/plan [message]` after selecting plan mode. The executor only admits attachments into durable objects; the declaring producer decides whether and how they become model-visible message content.

## Diagnosis summary

The UI "doesn't work at all" because of client-half defects (index.js host half is verified correct against the shipped runtime):

1. **Fatal — inject hook shape**: In the occupant registration, `hooks: { factoryState: (standard) => () => ... }` passes a *function*. Entry-owned inject faces convert `hooks.<name>` via `observableHook(source)` (`bindSnapshotSelector`), which needs `{ getSnapshot, subscribe }`. At body render, `useFactoryState()` → `useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector` calls `source.subscribe` → TypeError → the slot entry crashes inside its error boundary → the tab body never renders (blank / `data-slot-error` div).

2. **Fatal — selector required**: the bound hook is `useSelector(sel, eq)`; calling it without an identity selector crashes (`sel(snapshot)` with `sel === undefined`).

3. **Fatal — unreachable tab**: the tab type is a page type with no `guide` entry and no `patterns`; nothing ever opens `kind: 'factory'`. Even with rendering fixed, the user cannot open the Factory tab. Shipped page types (files, terminal…) contribute a `guide` entry; picking the capsule calls `openTab(entry.kind)`.

4. **Wrong sessionId plumbing**: `inject` receives the session binding key (the sessionId) as first argument — `(sessionId) => ...`. The `(standard) => ...` indirection in the current code assumed dispatcher-face semantics (function factories are only valid on the parent-declared dispatcher face like `tabInfo`).

5. **Minor — duplicate `t`**: registration declares `locale: NS` (the renderer's locale seat already provides a bound `t` prop) AND inject returns `t`. Shipped plugins do the former only. Drop `t` from the inject face.

Also the `useFactoryView` hook (useSyncExternalStore + useCallback juggling) is replaced by the framework's selector hook entirely.

## Fix design (client.js)

- Keep the envelope: ModuleLoader.load, exports.apply/inject = ['sidebarRightTabs','slots','locale','sessions'].
- Tab type: add `guide: [{ id: 'factory', order: 30, title, description, icon: FactoryGlyph }]`. Order: files=10, terminal=? (check quickly — sidebar-terminal guide order… not critical; pick 30).
- Body registration:
```js
ctx.slots.inject('sidebar.right.pane.tab', () => ctx.slots.register({
    name: 'sidebar.right.pane.tab',
    key: TAB_ID,
    locale: NS,
    inject: (sessionId) => ({
        hooks: {
            factoryState: ctx.sessions.binding(sessionId)?.session?.projections?.faceOf(PROJECTION_KEY) ?? absentFace,
        },
    }),
}, FactoryTabBody));
```
where `const absentFace = { getSnapshot: () => undefined, subscribe: () => () => {} }`.

Wait — careful: `faceOf` is on `binding.session.projections` — per goal: `sessions.binding(sessionId)?.session.projections.faceOf("goal")`. Use optional chaining; `faceOf` itself is always defined on a live binding.

But hmm — one subtlety: is `faceOf` truly always defined? The projection-store comment says "Always defined — absence is an undefined snapshot". `binding.session.projections` — the `session` object of the binding exposes `.projections` (a ProjectionValueStore). Optional-chain anyway + absent fallback for safety.

- Body component:
```js
function FactoryTabBody({ useTabInfo, useFactoryState, t }) {
    const view = useFactoryState(identity);
    ...same rendering...
}
```
`identity = (value) => value`. Hmm — but wait: does the locale seat give `t` even when the occupant has `locale: NS`? Jobs: yes. But let me double check the `t` seat binding in the renderer to be safe — "Locale `t` seat bindings, cached per (face, namespace, revision)" around line 513-560 of renderer client.js. <content>
1: # dsh-software-factory
2: 
3: A DSH (DeepSeek Harness) Host plugin bundle that adds the **`/factory <request>`**
4: slash command: a managed software-delivery pipeline with exactly eight phases,
5: executed by the session's agent through DSH-native machinery.
6: 
7: ```
8: /factory Add CSV export to the settings page
9: ```
10: 
11: The command steers one model-visible user message into the receiving agent —
12: the same mechanism `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode` uses for `/plan [message]` —
13: containing a structured pipeline prompt plus the user's request, then returns
14: a short success text. The agent runs the pipeline and narrates progress with
15: compact per-phase status lines such as:
16: 
17: ```
18: [factory] phase 3/8 implement: 3 tasks done
19: ```
20: 
21: ## The eight phases
22: 
23: | # | Key | Phase | Driven by |
24: |---|-----|-------|-----------|
25: | 1 | `capture` | Capture the request | restate goal, deliverables, constraints; derive acceptance criteria; ask only on material ambiguity |
26: | 2 | `plan` | Plan the tasks | the session's planning facilities: todo list (one todo per task), or `exit_plan_mode` in plan mode; each task names its write scope |
27: | 3 | `implement` | Implement the tasks | file tools (read/edit/write); for larger scopes, one subagent per task with disjoint write scopes |
28: | 4 | `guardrails` | Run guardrails (lint, typecheck, format check) | configured commands via the shell tool; long runs as background jobs; non-zero exit = failure |
29: | 5 | `test` | Test the implementation | configured test commands the same way, plus local/manual checks where possible |
30: | 6 | `deploy` | Deploy to a test environment | **only** when `deploy.enabled` and `deploy.command` are configured; otherwise explicitly skipped |
31: | 7 | `regression` | Run regression tests | the configured regression suite; regressions compared against phase-5 results |
32: | 8 | `evaluate` | Evaluate and report | evaluate against the original request; summarize evidence and limitations; present deliverables |
33: 
34: Enabled phases may not be skipped: failures are fixed and retried within the
35: phase, or reported honestly. Disabled phases are still announced with a
36: `skipped` status line. Command results are reported honestly — a non-zero
37: exit code is a failure.
38: 
39: When a command list (guardrails / tests / regression) is not configured, the
40: prompt tells the agent to discover the repository's standard checks and run
41: those, and to state clearly when none exist.
42: 
43: ## Install
44: 
45: Reviewed and installed by the Lead with the `plugin_manager` tool:
46: 
47: ```
48: action: install_bundle
49: target: <absolute path of this repository>
50: ```
51: 
52: The bundle inserts one row (`id: software-factory`) and needs no
53: dependencies, install scripts, or build tools.
54: 
55: ## Configuration
56: 
57: All keys are optional. Defaults: **every phase enabled except deploy** (deploy
58: stays off until both `deploy.enabled` is true and a `deploy.command` is set).
59: 
60: ```yaml
61: - id: software-factory
62:   name: '@local/dsh-software-factory'
63:   config:
64:     plan: true                    # phase 2 toggle
65:     implement: true               # phase 3 toggle
66:     guardrails: true              # phase 4 toggle
67:     test: true                    # phase 5 toggle
68:     regression: true              # phase 7 toggle
69:     evaluate: true                # phase 8 toggle
70:     subagentImplementation: true  # prefer per-task subagent delegation in phase 3
71:     guardrailCommand: 'npm run lint'        # string or array of strings
72:     testCommand: ['npm run typecheck', 'npm test']
73:     regressionCommand: 'npm run test:e2e'
74:     deploy:
75:       enabled: false
76:       command: './scripts/deploy-test.sh'
77: ```
78: 
79: Notes:
80: 
81: - Command fields accept one string or an array of non-empty strings; each
82:   entry runs as its own shell invocation in phase order.
83: - Unknown config keys fail at plugin activation (typos never silently
84:   disable a phase).
85: - A later patch layer overriding this row replaces `config` wholesale —
86:   restate every field you need (Cordis loader semantics).
87: 
88: ## Per-project configuration: `.factory.yml`
89: 
90: Each repository can override the phase switches and append per-phase prompt
91: instructions, without touching the profile. When `/factory` runs, the plugin
92: reads `.factory.yml` from the session workspace root (the session's working
93: directory) at command time — the same resolution the shipped
94: `dsh-agent-instructions` uses for AGENTS.md discovery.
95: 
96: **Merge order**: plugin row Config (global defaults) ← `.factory.yml`
97: (project overrides). File phase toggles win; command lists
98: (`guardrailCommand` etc.) and the deploy gate (`deploy.enabled` +
99: `deploy.command`) stay plugin-Config-only. A missing file changes nothing.
100: An **invalid file fails loudly**: the command returns an error naming the
101: file, its line, and the problem, and the pipeline does not start.
102: 
103: Full example (`.factory.yml` at the repository root):
104: 
105: ```yaml
106: # Per-project overrides for the /factory pipeline.
107: phases:
108:   plan: true
109:   implement: true
110:   guardrails: true
111:   test: true
112:   regression: false      # this repo has no regression suite yet
113:   evaluate: true
114: 
115: phasePrompts:
116:   plan: |
117:     Split backend and frontend tasks; the API contract in docs/api.md is
118:     authoritative.
119:   guardrails: |
120:     Run in this order:
121:     1. pnpm lint
122:     2. pnpm typecheck
123:     Never auto-fix formatting; report and stop.
124:   test: |
125:     Use `pnpm test --filter core` for unit tests; integration tests need the
126:     docker compose stack from scripts/dev.sh — start it as a background job.
127:   deploy: 'Deploy with ./scripts/deploy-test.sh, then curl the /healthz endpoint'
128:   evaluate: >-
129:     Include a section listing every changed file with a one-line rationale.
130: ```
131: 
132: `phasePrompts.<phase>` is appended **verbatim** to that phase's generated
133: prompt section, but only when the phase actually runs (a disabled phase's
134: prompt override is not used; `deploy` prompt text applies only while deploy
135: is active via plugin Config).
136: 
137: ### Supported format (strict subset)
138: 
139: The file is parsed by a dependency-free parser that accepts exactly this
140: subset — anything else is a loud, named error:
141: 
142: - Blank lines and `#` comments anywhere; UTF-8 BOM and CRLF tolerated; tabs
143:   in indentation are rejected.
144: - Two top-level mapping headers, each at most once, nothing after the colon:
145:   `phases:` and `phasePrompts:`.
146: - Nested entries at one consistent indentation (spaces only),
147:   `key: value` on a single line.
148: - `phases.<key>` ∈ `plan | implement | guardrails | test | regression |
149:   evaluate`, value exactly `true` or `false` (`yes`/`True` are errors — be
150:   explicit).
151: - `phasePrompts.<key>` ∈ `plan | implement | guardrails | test | deploy |
152:   regression | evaluate` (note: no `capture` — phase 1 is the request
153:   itself), value a string in one of these forms:
154:   - plain scalar — rest of the line, trimmed; a trailing ` # comment` is
155:     stripped;
156:   - `'single quoted'` (only escape: `''` → `'`) or `"double quoted"`
157:     (only escapes: `\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\t`), single line;
158:   - block scalar `|` or `|-` (literal: line breaks preserved) or `>` or
159:     `>-` (folded: paragraph lines joined with one space, each blank-line run
160:     collapses to one paragraph break, deeper-indented lines stay verbatim).
161:     `|`/`>` keep exactly one trailing newline; `|-`/`>-` strip trailing
162:     newlines.
163: - Not supported (loud errors): lists, anchors/aliases, tags, multi-document
164:   input, multi-line plain scalars, deeper nesting, empty values.
165: - Size cap: 65536 chars — the content becomes part of the steered prompt.
166: 
167: ## Right-sidebar progress tab (Web client)
168: 
169: The Web client gains a **Factory** tab in the right sidebar. It lists the
170: eight phases with live status (pending / active / done / skipped / failed),
171: shows the latest `[factory] phase …` narration line verbatim, and sits quiet
172: with an empty state while no run is active.
173: 
174: - **State source**: the Host's `factory` session projection folds
175:   `assistant/message` session-log events, matching ONLY lines that start
176:   with the plugin's own narration contract
177:   (`[factory] phase <n>/8 <key>: <status>`). The wire view reaches the
178:   client through the shipped session binding
179:   (`sessions.binding(id).session.projections.faceOf('factory')`) — the same
180:   host→client shape the shipped plan-mode and goal plugins use. Because it
181:   is a session projection, resume and fork restore the progress view.
182: - **Registration** (client half, `client.js`): one tab type through
183:   `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register({ id, kind, priority, title })` (the public
184:   two-stage path; the tab opens by kind like the shipped guide tab), plus
185:   the body and chip occupants in the `sidebar.right.pane.tab` /
186:   `sidebar.right.pane.tab.title` slots. Occupants receive the framework's
187:   `useTabInfo` hook plus this plugin's `useFactoryState` hook.
188: - **Styling**: theme tokens only (`--dsw-alias-*`, `--dsw-radius-*`,
189:   `--dsw-font-mono`); React from the browser module table; no Harness
190:   client package is imported.
191: - **Visibility**: client text is English constants + a Chinese dictionary
192:   registered with the client locale service (namespace `softwareFactory`).
193: 
194: ## Design notes
195: 
196: - **Command registration**: `ctx.commands.register({ name: 'factory',
197:   description, input: { hint: '<request>', attachments: true },
198:   recordInput: false, handler })` — the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-commands`
199:   contract. `recordInput: false` because the steered pipeline message already
200:   carries the request verbatim in the session log. The handler is async
201:   (the registry awaits its result) so it can read `.factory.yml` first.
202: - **Workspace root + file read**: `agent.session.header.cwd ?? process.cwd()`
203:   for the root, then the optional `fs` service
204:   (`resolve(name, { cwd, signal })` → `stat` → `readText`) with a `node:fs`
205:   fallback — the exact pattern the shipped `dsh-agent-instructions` uses for
206:   instruction files. The command's abort signal is honored throughout.
207: - **Submission**: `agent.steer(userMessage)` — inserts the message for the
208:   next step and wakes the driver. The message is built locally in the exact
209:   shape of dsh-llm's `createUserMessage` (`{ role, content, source: { kind:
210:   'user' }, id }`, deep-frozen); the identity brand is a compile-time no-op,
211:   so the bundle carries zero runtime dependencies.
212: - **Optional service**: the command is registered inside
213:   `ctx.inject(['commands'], ...)`, so the plugin stays dormant in profiles
214:   without the command surface instead of throwing. The `fs` service is a
215:   dynamic `ctx.get('fs')` lookup (also the agent-instructions pattern), not a
216:   static injection, so it remains an optimization path only.
217: - **YAML subset**: `.factory.yml` is parsed by an in-module strict parser
218:   (`parseFactoryYml`, exported for reuse/testing) documented above; no YAML
219:   dependency. Invalid input is a named-file, named-line error, and the
220:   command refuses to start the pipeline rather than silently ignoring the
221:   file.
222: - **Config schema**: `export const Config` implements the Standard Schema
223:   `~standard.validate` protocol that Cordis `resolveConfig` calls. Being
224:   vendor-unknown, Settings surfaces that project known schema vendors will

slash command: a managed software-delivery pipeline with exactly eight phases,
executed by the session's agent through DSH-native machinery.

The command steers one model-visible user message into the receiving agent —
containing a structured pipeline prompt plus the user's request, then returns
a short success text. The agent runs the pipeline and narrates progress with
compact per-phase status lines such as:
| 1 | `capture` | Capture the request | restate goal, deliverables, constraints; derive acceptance criteria; ask only on material ambiguity |
| 2 | `plan` | Plan the tasks | the session's planning facilities: todo list (one todo per task), or `exit_plan_mode` in plan mode; each task names its write scope |
| 3 | `implement` | Implement the tasks | file tools (read/edit/write); for larger scopes, one subagent per task with disjoint write scopes |
| 4 | `guardrails` | Run guardrails (lint, typecheck, format check) | configured commands via the shell tool; long runs as background jobs; non-zero exit = failure |
| 5 | `test` | Test the implementation | configured test commands the same way, plus local/manual checks where possible |
| 6 | `deploy` | Deploy to a test environment | **only** when `deploy.enabled` and `deploy.command` are configured; otherwise explicitly skipped |
| 7 | `regression` | Run regression tests | the configured regression suite; regressions compared against phase-5 results |
| 8 | `evaluate` | Evaluate and report | evaluate against the original request; summarize evidence and limitations; present deliverables |
Enabled phases may not be skipped: failures are fixed and retried within the
phase, or reported honestly. Disabled phases are still announced with a
`skipped` status line. Command results are reported honestly — a non-zero

Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: team_task_create
tools.description: Create one unowned pending task on the shared Team task board.

description.description: Complete task details and acceptance criteria.

blocked_by.description: Task ids that must complete first.

write_scopes.description: Advisory workspace-relative file or directory prefixes this task expects to modify.

tools.name: team_task_get
tools.description: Read the complete latest value of one shared task before changing or executing it.

tools.name: team_task_list
tools.description: List shared tasks, including readiness, owner, revision, blockers, and write-scope warnings.

owner.description: Optional member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents, matching ownerName; use unowned for tasks without an owner.

limit.description: Number of rows, 1 through 100. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: team_task_update
tools.description: Compare-and-set a shared task action using the latest revision from team_task_get or team_task_list.

expected_revision.description: Current task revision used as the CAS precondition.

write_scopes.description: Replacement advisory write scopes for edit.

owner.description: Member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents for Lead-only reassign; omit to unassign.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for the next teammate status, mailbox, or shared-task change after this call starts. This never wakes inactive members and returns noProgress immediately when no other member is running or provisioning. Re-list after wakeup or timeout instead of polling.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

Now the final report. Let me summarize:

## Why the UI didn't work
Diagnosed against the shipped DSH runtime (extracted the `dsh` subtree from `app.asar` into `.tmp/dsh`, 10,915 files, and cross-checked every contract). The host half (`/factory` command + `factory` session projection) was correct. The client half had three fatal defects:

1. **The tab could never render** — `client.js` passed a *function* as `hooks.factoryState` in the occupant's `inject()` face. The shipped renderer (`dsh-client-ui-renderer`) binds entry-owned `hooks.<name>` values with `observableHook(source)` → `useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector`, which requires an observable `{ getSnapshot, subscribe }` (function-valued hook factories are only valid on parent-declared dispatcher faces like `tabInfo`). At body render, `source.subscribe` was `undefined` → the slot entry crashed in its error boundary → blank tab. Fixed: `inject(sessionId)` now returns the projection face itself (`sessions.binding(sessionId).session.projections.faceOf('factory')` — always defined for a live binding; `undefined` snapshot = capability absent) with an absent-observable fallback for a missing binding (client.js:257).

2. **The selector hook was called without a selector** — even with a proper observable, the bound hook is `useSelector(sel, eq)`; a bare `useFactoryState()` call crashes inside uSES. Fixed at client.js:188 with `useFactoryState(identity)`.

3. **The tab was unreachable** — the tab type was a page type (`kind: 'factory'`, no `patterns`), and nothing anywhere opens a page type except the guide: picking a guide capsule calls `openTab(kind)`. Without a `guide` entry the Factory tab could never be opened. Fixed: the type now contributes a guide entry (client.js:243) with title/description/glyph, so it appears in the sidebar's guide page and the "+" strip control.

Plus one bug the smoke run caught in the host fold: a run abandoned mid-failure kept `running: true` (only a phase-8 line settles it), so the fresh-run reset — gated on `!running` — never fired, and a stale `failed` phase row survived into the next run. A phase-1 line now always opens a fresh board (index.js:175), with `stateVersion` bumped to 2 (index.js:241) so any stale cached rows are discarded and refolded.

Also removed the duplicate `t` delivery (the registration's `locale: NS` already provides the bound `t` prop; shipped plugins don't duplicate it), and updated README.md's registration section to the real contracts.

## What was verified correct and left alone
- Host: `sessionProjections.register` with a dynamic key + `{parse}` schema facades, `wire` for any key, unfiltered snapshot/onChanged wire to the client; commands contract; `agent.steer` + hand-rolled `createUserMessage`-shaped frozen message; `.factory.yml` reader.
- Client: ModuleLoader envelope, `exports.apply`/`inject`, `dsh.client` manifest (`platform` + `inject` = package deps loaded before consumers), CSS-tag pattern, two-stage tab registration path.

## Verification evidence (this turn)
- `node --check client.js` → exit 0; `node --check index.js` → exit 0.
- `.tmp/smoke.mjs` → `SMOKE PASS` — 48 behavioral checks: client bundle mount, tab-type + guide entry, keyed seat registrations, observable inject face (present + absent), body rendering for live/pristine/absent wire views, title chip; host config defaults + unknown-key rejection, `.factory.yml` parsing, project overrides, projection fold of a full run (statuses, finish, lastLine), failure + fresh-run semantics, command handler success/usage-error, steered message shape (frozen, `{role:'user', source:{kind:'user'}, id}`).

- Then run `/factory <request>` and open the Factory tab from the sidebar's "+" / guide page; it shows the 8 phases live.
